_**Agent (2026-06-04 08:32:59Z)**_

Short answer: **not yet** — audio-to-text is planned but not implemented.

Here's the state of it in Atelier:

**What's documented/planned (but not built):**
- A **Whisper sidecar on port 8766** using `mlx-whisper` with `whisper-large-v3-turbo` (~1.6 GB)
- Planned endpoints: `POST /transcribe` (sync, short clips) and `POST /transcribe/batch` (hour-long inputs with SSE job tracking)
- A planned `transcribe(file) → text` wrapper in the media toolkit PRD
- Referenced in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/ATELIER.md` (marked **"planned"**), and `docs/PRD-atelier-media-toolkit.md`

**What's actually running today** — all of these are **TTS (text→audio)**, the opposite direction:
- OmniVoice (8770), Kokoro (8765), Dia 1.6B (8769)

So right now Atelier can do **text → speech**, but there's no **speech → text** sidecar yet. Per the architecture doc, Whisper was deliberately deferred until after Kokoro and the video-gen proof-of-concept.

Want me to scaffold the whisper sidecar (the `sidecars/whisper/` FastAPI service per the architecture spec)? It's a well-defined plan in the docs, so I could stand it up.

float, sep: str) -> str:\n    ms = int(round(seconds * 1000))\n    h, ms = divmod(ms, 3_600_000)\n    m, ms = divmod(ms, 60_000)\n    s, ms = divmod(ms, 1000)\n    return t0\n    # Telemetry line the governor ingests (one observable pane). audio_s is the\n    # natural ASR ETA unit (seconds of audio -> seconds of compute).\n    segs = result.get(\"segments\", [])\n    audio_s = segs[-1][\"end\"] if segs else 0.0\n    chars = len(result.get(\"text\", \"\"))\n    rtf = (audio_s / elapsed) if elapsed > 0 else 0.0\n    print(f\"[asr] audio_s={audio_s:.1f} chars={chars} bytes={audio_bytes} \"\n          f\"{elapsed:.2f}s rtf={rtf:.1f}x lang={result.get('language')}\", flush=True)\n    return result, elapsed\n\n\n# ---------- HTTP: health ----------\n@app.get(\"/healthz\")\ndef healthz():\n    return {\"ok\": True, \"service\": \"whisper\", \"model\": MODEL_REPO, \"version\": \"1.0\"}\n\n\n@app.get(\"/readyz\")\ndef readyz():\n    state = \"warm\" if _loaded else \"cold\"\n    lifecycle = \"cold\" if not _loaded else (\"busy\" if _active > 0 else \"idle\")\n    return {\n        \"ok\": True,\n        \"state\": state,\n        \"lifecycle\": lifecycle,\n        \"busy\": _active > 0,\n        \"active_jobs\": _active,\n        \"queue_depth\": _waiting,\n        \"warmed\": _loaded,\n        \"model\": MODEL_REPO,\n        \"device\": \"mps\",\n        \"batch_jobs\": len(_jobs),\n        \"idle_seconds\": round(time.monotonic() - 0 and not force:\n        return {\"unloaded\": False, \"refused\": \"busy\", \"active_jobs\": _active}\n    was_loaded = _loaded\n    if was_loaded:\n        async with _sem:\n            await _unload_model()\n    return {\"unloaded\": was_loaded, \"forced\": force, \"model\": MODEL_REPO}\n\n\n# ---------- HTTP: sync transcribe ----------\n@app.post(\"/transcribe\")\nasync def transcribe(\n Form(default=None),\n    initial_prompt: str | None = Form(default=None),\n    word_timestamps: bool = Form(default=False),\n    response_format: str = Form(default=\"json\"),\n    save: bool = {"file_path":"/Users/gyasisutton/Documents/code/atelier/sidecars/whisper/README.md","content":"# whisper-sidecar — ASR (speech → text)\n\n`whisper-large-v3-turbo` via [`mlx-whisper`](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-examples/tree/main/whisper) on Apple MLX. Port **8766**. Part of the Mac Studio inference hub — see `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §5.2.\n\nOn an M1 Max: ~40–50× realtime (≈12 min of audio in ~15s).\n\n## Install / deploy\n\nHandled by `deploy/install.sh` (creates the venv, installs `requirements.txt`, symlinks `server.py` into `~/services/whisper-sidecar/`, drops the launchd plist, bootstraps the service).\n\nOne host prerequisite the other sidecars don't need — **ffmpeg**, which mlx-whisper shells out to for decoding mp3/m4a/etc.:\n\n```sh\nbrew install ffmpeg\n```\n\nThe model (~1.6 GB) auto-downloads into `HF_HOME` on the first `/transcribe`.\n\n## Input — three ways the audio can arrive\n\nPick **exactly one** of `file`, `url`, `path` per request.\n\n```sh\n# 1) UPLOAD the bytes (multipart)\ncurl -s :8766/transcribe -F file=@meeting.m4a\n\n# 2) PULL from a link — the sidecar downloads it itself\ncurl -s :8766/transcribe -F url=https://example.com/episode.mp3\n\n# 3) POINT at a file already on the Mac (no copy, no upload)\ncurl -s :8766/transcribe -F path=/Users/gyasisutton/outputs/podcast/ep12.wav\n```\n\n## Output — what comes back, and where it's saved\n\nThe transcript is **always returned inline**; `response_format` picks the shape, and `save=true` *also* writes it to disk.\n\n```sh\n# default: lean JSON {text, language, segments[]}\ncurl -s :8766/transcribe -F path=/path/a.wav\n\n# plain text / subtitles\ncurl -s :8766/transcribe -F path=/path/a.wav -F response_format=text\ncurl -s :8766/transcribe -F path=/path/a.wav -F response_format=srt\ncurl -s :8766/transcribe -F path=/path/a.wav -F response_format=vtt\n# verbose_json = full whisper segments (tokens, logprobs, …)\n\n# ALSO save to disk. Default location: $WHISPER_OUTPUT_DIR/<sha256>.<ext>\ncurl -s :8766/transcribe -F path=/path/a.wav -F save=true -F response_format=srt\n# …or an explicit destination:\ncurl -s :8766/transcribe -F path=/path/a.wav -F save=true -F output_path=/Users/gyasisutton/outputs/a.json\n```\n\nEvery response carries **`x-content-sha256`** (the cache key for that audio — matches the gateway's transcript cache in `ARCHITECTURE.md` §4) and `x-saved-path` when saved.\n\nOptional form fields: `language` (ISO code, else auto-detect), `initial_prompt` (bias spelling/terms), `word_timestamps=true`.\n\n## Long audio — async batch\n\nFor hour-long inputs, submit a job (source is `url` or `path`) and stream progress:\n\n```sh\nJOB=$(curl -s :8766/transcribe/batch -H 'content-type: application/json' \\\n  -d '{\"path\":\"/Users/gyasisutton/outputs/long-show.wav\",\"response_format\":\"srt\"}' | jq -r .job_id)\n\ncurl -N :8766/jobs/$JOB/stream      # SSE: status → heartbeat → result\ncurl -s  :8766/jobs/$JOB/result     # the transcript once done\ncurl -s  -X DELETE :8766/jobs/$JOB  # cancel (only before it starts running)\n```\n\nBatch jobs `save=true` by default, so the result survives a client disconnect.\n\n> Per-segment streaming progress is a v2 item — mlx-whisper has no progress callback in the stable release, so the SSE stream emits coarse status + heartbeats, then the final result.\n\n## Health & lifecycle\n\n| Endpoint | Purpose |\n|---|---|\n| `GET /healthz` | liveness |\n| `GET /readyz` | warm/cold/busy, `active_jobs`, `queue_depth`, `batch_jobs` |\n| `POST /admin/unload[?force=true]` | drop the model from memory (governor courtesy) |\n\nLike the other sidecars, the model **idle-unloads after 5 min** (`IDLE_UNLOAD_SECONDS`, override with `KEEP_WARM=true`) so a 1.6 GB model doesn't squat on unified memory between bursts. The governor (`:8799`) tails this sidecar's `[asr]` log lines, so transcribe calls show up in the hub's telemetry and feed the ETA predictor (`kind=asr`, `audio_s` → compute seconds).\n\n## Env vars\n\n| Var | Default |\n|---|---|\n| `WHISPER_MODEL_REPO` | `mlx-community/whisper-large-v3-turbo` |\n| `WHISPER_OUTPUT_DIR` | `~/outputs/transcripts` |\n| `WHISPER_MAX_PULL_MB` | `512` (cap on url-pulled audio) |\n| `IDLE_UNLOAD_SECONDS` | `300` |\n| `KEEP_WARM` | `false` |\n| `HUB_TOKEN` | unset (set → work endpoints require `Authorization: Bearer …`) |\n| `HF_HOME` | shared hub cache |\n"}

The sidecar keeps ONE model resident and hot-swaps when a request\nasks for a different one (memory courtesy — large-v3 ~3 GB vs turbo ~1.6 GB).\nThe governor learns a separate ETA per model, so a caller can trade speed\n(turbo) against accuracy (large) on real numbers.\n    model=turbo     -> mlx-community/whisper-large-v3-turbo   (default, fast)\n    model=large     -> mlx-community/whisper-large-v3         (slower, accurate)\n    model=accurate  -> mlx-community/whisper-large-v3\n    model=<hf/repo> -> any mlx-community whisper repo\nDefault when omitted: $WHISPER_MODEL_REPO.\n\nINPUT — three ways audio can arrive (pick exactly one per request):\n    file=@clip.m4a      multipart upload (the audio bytes themselves)\n    url=https://…/a.mp3 a link the sidecar pulls down itself\n    path=/Users/…/a.wav a file already on the Mac (no copy, no upload)\n\nOUTPUT — where the transcript goes:\n    response body          always returned inline (json | text | srt | vtt | verbose_json)\n    save=true              ALSO written to disk under WHISPER_OUTPUT_DIR, named by\n                           the sha256 of the audio bytes (matches the gateway's\n                           transcript cache key in ARCHITECTURE.md §4) — or to an\n                           explicit output_path if given.\n    x-content-sha256       header on every response — the cache key for that audio.\n\nEndpoints:\n    GET  /healthz              liveness\n    GET  /readyz               status (warm/cold/busy), resident model, queue depth\n    GET  /models               available aliases + which is loaded\n    POST /admin/unload         force-unload the model (memory-governor courtesy)\n    POST /transcribe           sync; for clips under ~a few minutes\n    POST /transcribe/batch     async; returns {job_id} for long audio\n    GET  /jobs/<id>            job status snapshot\n    GET  /jobs/<id>/stream     SSE progress: queued -> running -> done/error\n    GET  /jobs/<id>/result     the transcript once done\n    DELETE /jobs/<id>          cancel a job (only effective before it starts running)\n\nEnv vars:\n    WHISPER_MODEL_REPO    default model when a request omits `model`,\n                          default \"mlx-community/whisper-large-v3-turbo\"\n    WHISPER_OUTPUT_DIR    where save=true writes, default ~/outputs/transcripts\n    WHISPER_MAX_PULL_MB   cap on url-pulled audio, default 512\n    HF_HOME               model cache (shared hub cache)\n    HUB_TOKEN             optional bearer token; if set, work endpoints require it\n    IDLE_UNLOAD_SECONDS   unload after N idle seconds, default 300\n    KEEP_WARM             \"true\" to disable idle-unload (default false — ASR is bursty)\n\"\"\"\n\nimport asyncio\nimport gc\nimport hashlib\nimport json\nimport os\nimport secrets\nimport tempfile\nimport time\nfrom contextlib import asynccontextmanager\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport httpx\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, File, Form, HTTPException, Request, UploadFile\nfrom fastapi.responses import JSONResponse, PlainTextResponse, StreamingResponse\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, Field\n\nimport mlx_whisper\n\nDEFAULT_MODEL = os.environ.get(\"WHISPER_MODEL_REPO\", \"mlx-community/whisper-large-v3-turbo\")\n# Caller-selectable models — the request decides which one Atelier loads.\nMODEL_ALIASES = {\n    \"turbo\": \"mlx-community/whisper-large-v3-turbo\",\n    \"large-turbo\": \"mlx-community/whisper-large-v3-turbo\",\n    \"large\": \"mlx-community/whisper-large-v3\",\n    \"large-v3\": \"mlx-community/whisper-large-v3\",\n    \"accurate\": \"mlx-community/whisper-large-v3\",\n}\nOUTPUT_DIR = Path(os.environ.get(\"WHISPER_OUTPUT_DIR\", str(Path.home() / \"outputs/transcripts\")))\nMAX_PULL_BYTES = int(os.environ.get(\"WHISPER_MAX_PULL_MB\", \"512\")) * 1024 * 1024\nHUB_TOKEN = os.environ.get(\"HUB_TOKEN\")\n# Constitutional idle-unload (see kokoro/dia): a multi-GB model squatting on\n# unified memory while idle starves video/LLM jobs. Default unload after 5 min.\n# KEEP_WARM=true opts out (e.g. a long batch transcription session).\nIDLE_UNLOAD_SECONDS = int(os.environ.get(\"IDLE_UNLOAD_SECONDS\", \"300\"))\nKEEP_WARM = os.environ.get(\"KEEP_WARM\", \"false\").lower() in (\"1\", \"true\", \"yes\")\nIDLE_TICK_SECONDS = 30\n\n# mlx-whisper loads via an lru_cache'd loader; we track load state ourselves\n# since that cache is opaque. _loaded_model = the HF repo currently resident\n# (None when unloaded). Exactly one model is kept resident at a time.\n_loaded_model: str | None = None\n_sem = asyncio.Semaphore(1)            # single-flight: MLX is single-stream on the GPU\n_last_request_at = time.monotonic()\n_unload_task: asyncio.Task | None = None\n_idle_unloaded_at: float | None = None\n# Job-aware state (memory governor): _active = transcriptions in flight (busy when\n# >0), _waiting = callers queued on the semaphore. The idle-watcher must NEVER\n# unload while _active>0 or _waiting>0 — a long batch must not be reaped mid-job.\n_active: int = 0\n_waiting: int = 0\n\n# Batch job registry. Jobs are in-process only (lost on restart) — fine for v1;\n# the gateway owns durable caching by sha256. id -> job dict.\n_jobs: dict[str, dict] = {}\n\n\ndef _resolve_model(name: str | None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Map a caller's `model` (alias or full repo) to an HF repo. None -> default.\"\"\"\n    if not name:\n        return DEFAULT_MODEL\n    return MODEL_ALIASES.get(name.strip().lower(), name.strip())\n\n\n# ---------- model lifecycle ----------\ndef _mlx_clear_cache() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Best-effort free of MLX's Metal buffer cache across mlx versions.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        import mlx.core as mx\n        if hasattr(mx, \"clear_cache\"):\n            mx.clear_cache()\n        elif hasattr(mx, \"metal\") and hasattr(mx.metal, \"clear_cache\"):\n            mx.metal.clear_cache()\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n\n\nasync def _load_and_warm(repo: str = DEFAULT_MODEL) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Cold-load `repo` into mlx-whisper's loader cache + warm it. Idempotent\n    for the same repo. Caller must hold _sem.\"\"\"\n    global _loaded_model, _idle_unloaded_at\n    if _loaded_model == repo:\n        return\n    t0 = time.perf_counter()\n    print(f\"[whisper] loading {repo}\", flush=True)\n    try:\n        await asyncio.to_thread(mlx_whisper.load_models.load_model, repo)\n        _loaded_model = repo\n        _idle_unloaded_at = None\n        print(f\"[whisper] model warm in {time.perf_counter()-t0:.1f}s ({repo})\", flush=True)\n    except Exception as e:\n        _loaded_model = None\n        print(f\"[whisper] load failed for {repo}: {e}\", flush=True)\n\n\nasync def _unload_model() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Drop the resident model by clearing mlx-whisper's loader cache. Caller\n    must hold _sem.\"\"\"\n    global _loaded_model, _idle_unloaded_at\n    if _loaded_model is None:\n        return\n    print(f\"[whisper] idle-unload — clearing model cache ({_loaded_model})\", flush=True)\n    try:\n        # The loader is @lru_cache'd; clearing it drops every cached model.\n        if hasattr(mlx_whisper.load_models.load_model, \"cache_clear\"):\n            mlx_whisper.load_models.load_model.cache_clear()\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f\"[whisper] cache_clear failed: {e}\", flush=True)\n    _loaded_model = None\n    _idle_unloaded_at = time.monotonic()\n    gc.collect()\n    _mlx_clear_cache()\n\n\nasync def _idle_watcher() -> None:\n    if KEEP_WARM:\n        print(\"[whisper] idle-watcher disabled (KEEP_WARM=true)\", flush=True)\n        return\n    print(f\"[whisper] idle-watcher active (unload after {IDLE_UNLOAD_SECONDS}s idle)\", flush=True)\n    while True:\n        await asyncio.sleep(IDLE_TICK_SECONDS)\n        if _loaded_model is None:\n            continue\n        if _active == 0 and _waiting == 0 and time.monotonic() - _last_request_at > IDLE_UNLOAD_SECONDS:\n            async with _sem:\n                if _loaded_model is not None and _active == 0:\n                    await _unload_model()\n\n\n@asynccontextmanager\nasync def lifespan(app: FastAPI):\n    global _unload_task\n    OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    async with _sem:\n        await _load_and_warm(DEFAULT_MODEL)\n    _unload_task = asyncio.create_task(_idle_watcher())\n    yield\n    if _unload_task and not _unload_task.done():\n        _unload_task.cancel()\n        try:\n            await _unload_task\n        except asyncio.CancelledError:\n            pass\n\n\napp = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)\n\n\ndef _check_auth(request: Request) -> None:\n    if not HUB_TOKEN:\n        return\n    auth = request.headers.get(\"authorization\", \"\")\n    if not auth.startswith(\"Bearer \") or auth[7:] != HUB_TOKEN:\n        raise HTTPException(401, \"invalid bearer token\")\n\n\n# ---------- source resolution (file | url | path) ----------\nasync def _resolve_source(\n    file: UploadFile | None, url: str | None, path: str | None\n) -> tuple[str, bytes, bool]:\n    \"\"\"Turn whichever input arrived into (local_path, raw_bytes, is_temp).\n\n    Exactly one of file/url/path must be provided. raw_bytes is what we sha256\n    for the cache key + output naming. is_temp marks files we must clean up.\n    \"\"\"\n    provided = [k for k, v in ((\"file\", file), (\"url\", url), (\"path\", path)) if v]\n    if len(provided) == 0:\n        raise HTTPException(400, \"provide exactly one of: file (upload), url (link), path (local file)\")\n    if len(provided) > 1:\n        raise HTTPException(400, f\"provide only one source, got: {', '.join(provided)}\")\n\n    if file is not None:\n        data = await file.read()\n        if not data:\n            raise HTTPException(400, \"uploaded file is empty\")\n        suffix = Path(file.filename or \"audio\").suffix or \".bin\"\n        fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=\"whisper-up-\", suffix=suffix)\n        os.write(fd, data)\n        os.close(fd)\n        return tmp, data, True\n\n    if url is not None:\n        try:\n            chunks = []\n            total = 0\n            async with httpx.AsyncClient(follow_redirects=True, timeout=60) as client:\n                async with client.stream(\"GET\", url) as resp:\n                    resp.raise_for_status()\n                    suffix = Path(httpx.URL(url).path).suffix or \".bin\"\n                    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=\"whisper-pull-\", suffix=suffix)\n                    with os.fdopen(fd, \"wb\") as out:\n                        async for chunk in resp.aiter_bytes():\n                            total += len(chunk)\n                            if total > MAX_PULL_BYTES:\n                                out.close()\n                                os.unlink(tmp)\n                                raise HTTPException(413, f\"pulled audio exceeds {MAX_PULL_BYTES // (1024*1024)} MB cap\")\n                            out.write(chunk)\n                            chunks.append(chunk)\n        except HTTPException:\n            raise\n        except Exception as e:\n            raise HTTPException(502, f\"could not pull url: {e}\")\n        return tmp, b\"\".join(chunks), True\n\n    # path: a file already on the Mac — no copy.\n    p = Path(path).expanduser()\n    if not p.is_file():\n        raise HTTPException(400, f\"path not found on host: {p}\")\n    return str(p), p.read_bytes(), False\n\n\n# ---------- transcript formatting + output ----------\ndef _ts(seconds: float, sep: str) -> str:\n    ms = int(round(seconds * 1000))\n    h, ms = divmod(ms, 3_600_000)\n    m, ms = divmod(ms, 60_000)\n    s, ms = divmod(ms, 1000)\n    return f\"{h:02d}:{m:02d}:{s:02d}{sep}{ms:03d}\"\n\n\ndef _to_srt(segments: list[dict]) -> str:\n    out = []\n    for i, seg in enumerate(segments, 1):\n        out.append(str(i))\n        out.append(f\"{_ts(seg['start'], ',')} --> {_ts(seg['end'], ',')}\")\n        out.append(seg[\"text\"].strip())\n        out.append(\"\")\n    return \"\\n\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _to_vtt(segments: list[dict]) -> str:\n    out = [\"WEBVTT\", \"\"]\n    for seg in segments:\n        out.append(f\"{_ts(seg['start'], '.')} --> {_ts(seg['end'], '.')}\")\n        out.append(seg[\"text\"].strip())\n        out.append(\"\")\n    return \"\\n\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _trim_segments(segments: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:\n    \"\"\"Keep the fields a caller actually uses; drop tokens/logprobs noise.\"\"\"\n    return [\n        {\"id\": s.get(\"id\"), \"start\": s.get(\"start\"), \"end\": s.get(\"end\"),\n         \"text\": s.get(\"text\", \"\").strip()}\n        for s in segments\n    ]\n\n\ndef _format_body(result: dict, fmt: str):\n    \"\"\"Return (payload, media_type) for the requested response_format.\"\"\"\n    segs = result.get(\"segments\", [])\n    if fmt == \"text\":\n        return result.get(\"text\", \"\").strip(), \"text/plain\"\n    if fmt == \"srt\":\n        return _to_srt(segs), \"application/x-subrip\"\n    if fmt == \"vtt\":\n        return _to_vtt(segs), \"text/vtt\"\n    if fmt == \"verbose_json\":\n        return result, \"application/json\"\n    # default \"json\": the lean {text, segments, language} shape from ARCHITECTURE §5.2\n    return {\"text\": result.get(\"text\", \"\").strip(),\n            \"language\": result.get(\"language\"),\n            \"segments\": _trim_segments(segs)}, \"application/json\"\n\n\ndef _save_output(result: dict, sha: str, fmt: str, output_path: str | None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Write the transcript to disk; return the path. Default name = sha256 of\n    the audio (the gateway's cache key), so re-transcribing the same bytes maps\n    to the same file.\"\"\"\n    ext = {\"text\": \"txt\", \"srt\": \"srt\", \"vtt\": \"vtt\"}.get(fmt, \"json\")\n    if output_path:\n        dest = Path(output_path).expanduser()\n        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    else:\n        OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n        dest = OUTPUT_DIR / f\"{sha}.{ext}\"\n    body, _ = _format_body(result, fmt)\n    if isinstance(body, (dict, list)):\n        dest.write_text(json.dumps(body, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))\n    else:\n        dest.write_text(body)\n    return str(dest)\n\n\ndef _transcribe_sync(audio_path: str, repo: str, language: str | None,\n                     initial_prompt: str | None, word_timestamps: bool) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Blocking mlx-whisper call. Runs in a thread off the event loop. `repo` is\n    already resident (pre-loaded under the semaphore), so transcribe's internal\n    loader hits the cache.\"\"\"\n    return mlx_whisper.transcribe(\n        audio_path,\n        path_or_hf_repo=repo,\n        language=language,\n        initial_prompt=initial_prompt,\n        word_timestamps=word_timestamps,\n    )\n\n\nasync def _run_transcription(audio_path: str, repo: str, language: str | None,\n                             initial_prompt: str | None, word_timestamps: bool,\n                             audio_bytes: int):\n    \"\"\"Ensure `repo` is the resident model (hot-swap if needed), then transcribe —\n    all under the single-flight semaphore so a swap can't race a job. Returns\n    (result, elapsed_seconds) and emits the [asr] telemetry line the governor\n    tails (tagged with the model, so ETAs are learned per model).\"\"\"\n    global _last_request_at, _active, _waiting\n    t0 = time.perf_counter()\n    _waiting += 1\n    async with _sem:\n        _waiting -= 1\n        _active += 1\n        try:\n            # The request decides which model is loaded. Swap if a different one\n            # is resident; cold-load if nothing is.\n            if _loaded_model != repo:\n                if _loaded_model is not None:\n                    await _unload_model()\n                await _load_and_warm(repo)\n                if _loaded_model != repo:\n                    raise HTTPException(503, f\"could not load model {repo}; see server logs\")\n            result = await asyncio.to_thread(\n                _transcribe_sync, audio_path, repo, language, initial_prompt, word_timestamps\n            )\n        except HTTPException:\n            raise\n        except Exception as e:\n            raise HTTPException(500, f\"transcription failed: {e}\")\n        finally:\n            _active -= 1\n            _last_request_at = time.monotonic()\n    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - t0\n    # Telemetry line the governor ingests (one observable pane). Tagged with the\n    # model so the predictor learns turbo vs large separately. audio_s is the\n    # natural ASR ETA unit (seconds of audio -> seconds of compute).\n    segs = result.get(\"segments\", [])\n    audio_s = segs[-1][\"end\"] if segs else 0.0\n    chars = len(result.get(\"text\", \"\"))\n    rtf = (audio_s / elapsed) if elapsed > 0 else 0.0\n    short = repo.split(\"/\")[-1]\n    print(f\"[asr] model={short} audio_s={audio_s:.1f} chars={chars} bytes={audio_bytes} \"\n          f\"{elapsed:.2f}s rtf={rtf:.1f}x lang={result.get('language')}\", flush=True)\n    return result, elapsed\n\n\n# ---------- HTTP: health ----------\n@app.get(\"/healthz\")\ndef healthz():\n    return {\"ok\": True, \"service\": \"whisper\", \"default_model\": DEFAULT_MODEL,\n            \"loaded_model\": _loaded_model, \"version\": \"1.1\"}\n\n\n@app.get(\"/readyz\")\ndef readyz():\n    state = \"warm\" if _loaded_model else \"cold\"\n    lifecycle = \"cold\" if not _loaded_model else (\"busy\" if _active > 0 else \"idle\")\n    return {\n        \"ok\": True,\n        \"state\": state,\n        \"lifecycle\": lifecycle,\n        \"busy\": _active > 0,\n        \"active_jobs\": _active,\n        \"queue_depth\": _waiting,\n        \"warmed\": _loaded_model is not None,\n        \"model\": _loaded_model or DEFAULT_MODEL,\n        \"loaded_model\": _loaded_model,\n        \"default_model\": DEFAULT_MODEL,\n        \"device\": \"mps\",\n        \"batch_jobs\": len(_jobs),\n        \"idle_seconds\": round(time.monotonic() - _last_request_at, 1),\n        \"idle_unload_seconds\": IDLE_UNLOAD_SECONDS,\n        \"keep_warm\": KEEP_WARM,\n        \"last_unload_ago_s\": round(time.monotonic() - _idle_unloaded_at, 1) if _idle_unloaded_at else None,\n    }\n\n\n@app.get(\"/models\")\ndef models(request: Request):\n    \"\"\"What can be requested, and what's resident right now. Lets a caller (or\n    the dashboard) decide which model to ask for.\"\"\"\n    _check_auth(request)\n    return {\n        \"aliases\": MODEL_ALIASES,\n        \"default\": DEFAULT_MODEL,\n        \"loaded\": _loaded_model,\n        \"note\": \"pass model=<alias|hf/repo> to /transcribe; the sidecar hot-swaps to it\",\n    }\n\n\n@app.post(\"/admin/unload\")\nasync def admin_unload(request: Request):\n    \"\"\"Force-unload now. Refuses while busy unless ?force=true (governor preempt).\"\"\"\n    _check_auth(request)\n    force = request.query_params.get(\"force\", \"\").lower() in (\"1\", \"true\", \"yes\")\n    if _active > 0 and not force:\n        return {\"unloaded\": False, \"refused\": \"busy\", \"active_jobs\": _active}\n    was = _loaded_model\n    if was is not None:\n        async with _sem:\n            await _unload_model()\n    return {\"unloaded\": was is not None, \"forced\": force, \"model\": was}\n\n\n# ---------- HTTP: sync transcribe ----------\n@app.post(\"/transcribe\")\nasync def transcribe(\n    request: Request,\n    file: UploadFile | None = File(default=None),\n    url: str | None = Form(default=None),\n    path: str | None = Form(default=None),\n    model: str | None = Form(default=None),\n    language: str | None = Form(default=None),\n    initial_prompt: str | None = Form(default=None),\n    word_timestamps: bool = Form(default=False),\n    response_format: str = Form(default=\"json\"),\n    save: bool = Form(default=False),\n    output_path: str | None = Form(default=None),\n):\n    \"\"\"Synchronous transcription for short clips (under ~a few minutes).\n\n    Model — `model` picks which whisper Atelier loads (alias turbo|large|accurate\n    or a full HF repo); omitted = WHISPER_MODEL_REPO. The sidecar hot-swaps to it.\n    Source — exactly one of: file (multipart upload), url (link to pull),\n    path (file already on the Mac).\n    Output — response body in response_format (json|text|srt|vtt|verbose_json);\n    set save=true to also persist it under WHISPER_OUTPUT_DIR (or output_path).\n    \"\"\"\n    _check_auth(request)\n    fmt = response_format.lower()\n    if fmt not in (\"json\", \"text\", \"srt\", \"vtt\", \"verbose_json\"):\n        raise HTTPException(400, f\"unknown response_format: {response_format}\")\n    repo = _resolve_model(model)\n\n    audio_path, raw, is_temp = await _resolve_source(file, url, path)\n    sha = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()\n    try:\n        result, elapsed = await _run_transcription(\n            audio_path, repo, language, initial_prompt, word_timestamps, len(raw)\n        )\n    finally:\n        if is_temp:\n            try:\n                os.unlink(audio_path)\n            except OSError:\n                pass\n\n    headers = {\"x-content-sha256\": sha, \"x-transcribe-seconds\": f\"{elapsed:.3f}\",\n               \"x-model\": repo}\n    if save:\n        headers[\"x-saved-path\"] = _save_output(result, sha, fmt, output_path)\n\n    body, media_type = _format_body(result, fmt)\n    if isinstance(body, (dict, list)):\n        return JSONResponse(content=body, headers=headers)\n    return PlainTextResponse(content=body, media_type=media_type, headers=headers)\n\n\n# ---------- HTTP: async batch ----------\nclass BatchReq(BaseModel):\n    url: str | None = None\n    path: str | None = None\n    model: str | None = None\n    language: str | None = None\n    initial_prompt: str | None = None\n    word_timestamps: bool = False\n    response_format: str = Field(default=\"json\")\n    save: bool = True\n    output_path: str | None = None\n\n\nasync def _run_job(job_id: str, req: BatchReq) -> None:\n    job = _jobs[job_id]\n    if job.get(\"cancel\"):\n        job.update(status=\"cancelled\", finished_at=time.time())\n        return\n    job.update(status=\"running\", started_at=time.time())\n    try:\n        repo = _resolve_model(req.model)\n        job[\"model\"] = repo\n        audio_path, raw, is_temp = await _resolve_source(None, req.url, req.path)\n        sha = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()\n        job[\"sha256\"] = sha\n        try:\n            result, elapsed = await _run_transcription(\n                audio_path, repo, req.language, req.initial_prompt, req.word_timestamps, len(raw)\n            )\n        finally:\n            if is_temp:\n                try:\n                    os.unlink(audio_path)\n                except OSError:\n                    pass\n        fmt = req.response_format.lower()\n        saved = _save_output(result, sha, fmt, req.output_path) if req.save else None\n        body, _ = _format_body(result, fmt)\n        job.update(status=\"done\", finished_at=time.time(), elapsed_s=round(elapsed, 3),\n                   saved_path=saved, result=body)\n    except HTTPException as e:\n        job.update(status=\"error\", finished_at=time.time(), error=f\"{e.status_code}: {e.detail}\")\n    except Exception as e:\n        job.update(status=\"error\", finished_at=time.time(), error=str(e))\n\n\n@app.post(\"/transcribe/batch\")\nasync def transcribe_batch(req: BatchReq, request: Request):\n    \"\"\"Submit a long transcription. Returns {job_id} immediately; poll\n    /jobs/<id> or stream /jobs/<id>/stream. Source is url or path (uploads go\n    through the sync endpoint). `model` selects the whisper to load. save\n    defaults to true — long jobs persist by sha256 so the result survives a\n    client disconnect.\"\"\"\n    _check_auth(request)\n    if not (req.url or req.path):\n        raise HTTPException(400, \"batch requires url or path\")\n    if req.url and req.path:\n        raise HTTPException(400, \"provide only one of url or path\")\n    job_id = secrets.token_hex(8)\n    _jobs[job_id] = {\"id\": job_id, \"status\": \"queued\", \"created_at\": time.time(),\n                     \"source\": req.url or req.path, \"model\": _resolve_model(req.model),\n                     \"cancel\": False}\n    asyncio.create_task(_run_job(job_id, req))\n    return {\"job_id\": job_id, \"status\": \"queued\"}\n\n\ndef _job_public(job: dict) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Job snapshot without the (potentially large) result payload.\"\"\"\n    return {k: v for k, v in job.items() if k not in (\"result\", \"cancel\")}\n\n\n@app.get(\"/jobs/{job_id}\")\ndef job_status(job_id: str, request: Request):\n    _check_auth(request)\n    job = _jobs.get(job_id)\n    if not job:\n        raise HTTPException(404, \"no such job\")\n    return _job_public(job)\n\n\n@app.get(\"/jobs/{job_id}/result\")\ndef job_result(job_id: str, request: Request):\n    _check_auth(request)\n    job = _jobs.get(job_id)\n    if not job:\n        raise HTTPException(404, \"no such job\")\n    if job[\"status\"] != \"done\":\n        raise HTTPException(409, f\"job not done (status={job['status']})\")\n    return {\"job_id\": job_id, \"sha256\": job.get(\"sha256\"), \"model\": job.get(\"model\"),\n            \"saved_path\": job.get(\"saved_path\"), \"result\": job.get(\"result\")}\n\n\n@app.get(\"/jobs/{job_id}/stream\")\nasync def job_stream(job_id: str, request: Request):\n    \"\"\"SSE progress for a batch job. Emits one event per status change plus a\n    heartbeat with elapsed seconds, then a terminal event (done/error/cancelled)\n    and closes. Real per-segment progress is a v2 enhancement — mlx-whisper has\n    no streaming callback in the stable release.\"\"\"\n    _check_auth(request)\n    if job_id not in _jobs:\n        raise HTTPException(404, \"no such job\")\n\n    async def gen():\n        last = None\n        while True:\n            job = _jobs.get(job_id)\n            if job is None:\n                yield f\"event: error\\ndata: {json.dumps({'error': 'job evicted'})}\\n\\n\"\n                return\n            status = job[\"status\"]\n            if status != last:\n                yield f\"event: status\\ndata: {json.dumps(_job_public(job))}\\n\\n\"\n                last = status\n            if status in (\"done\", \"error\", \"cancelled\"):\n                if status == \"done\":\n                    yield f\"event: result\\ndata: {json.dumps({'job_id': job_id, 'saved_path': job.get('saved_path'), 'elapsed_s': job.get('elapsed_s')})}\\n\\n\"\n                return\n            elapsed = round(time.time() - job.get(\"started_at\", job[\"created_at\"]), 1)\n            yield f\"event: heartbeat\\ndata: {json.dumps({'status': status, 'elapsed_s': elapsed})}\\n\\n\"\n            await asyncio.sleep(1.0)\n\n    return StreamingResponse(gen(), media_type=\"text/event-stream\")\n\n\n@app.delete(\"/jobs/{job_id}\")\ndef job_cancel(job_id: str, request: Request):\n    \"\"\"Cancel a job. Effective only before it starts running — mlx-whisper\n    can't be interrupted mid-call, so a running job runs to completion.\"\"\"\n    _check_auth(request)\n    job = _jobs.get(job_id)\n    if not job:\n        raise HTTPException(404, \"no such job\")\n    if job[\"status\"] == \"queued\":\n        job[\"cancel\"] = True\n        job[\"status\"] = \"cancelled\"\n        return {\"cancelled\": True, \"job_id\": job_id}\n    return {\"cancelled\": False, \"job_id\": job_id, \"reason\": f\"already {job['status']}\"}\n"}

_**Agent (2026-06-04 09:44:14Z)**_

All green. Here's what changed to make the model **a per-request parameter** instead of hardcoded:

**Sidecar (`sidecars/whisper/server.py`)**
- New `model=` form/JSON param on `/transcribe` and `/transcribe/batch`. Accepts an **alias** (`turbo` → large-v3-turbo, `large`/`accurate` → large-v3) or a **full HF repo**. Omitted → `$WHISPER_MODEL_REPO`.
- The sidecar keeps **exactly one model resident** and **hot-swaps** when a request asks for a different one — the swap (unload old → load new) happens *inside* the single-flight semaphore, so it can never race an in-flight job. This is the "Atelier decides what to load" behavior: the request carries the signal, the sidecar acts on it.
- New `GET /models` — lists aliases + which model is currently loaded (so a caller/dashboard can see and choose).
- `/readyz` now reports `loaded_model`, `default_model`. Telemetry line is tagged: `[asr] model=<variant> …`.

**Governor**
- `[asr]` parser now captures the `model=` tag and records ETAs **per model** (`predictor.record(kind="asr", model=<variant>)`). So turbo and large accumulate separate histories.
- `/estimate?engine=whisper&model=whisper-large-v3&audio_s=720` returns a learned ETA for that specific variant — the data a caller uses to decide speed vs accuracy.

**Predictor** — `asr` is a first-class kind (rate = sec per audio-second), with separate priors so each whisper variant learns independently.

So nothing's hardcoded: the request picks the model, the sidecar loads/swaps to it, and the governor learns per-model timing so the choice can be made on real numbers. The `WHISPER_MODEL_REPO` env var only sets the *default* when a request doesn't specify one.

_**Agent (2026-06-04 09:46:10Z)**_

Yes, that makes sense. You want two **optional post-processing methods** layered on top of the raw transcript, both powered by the hub's local LLM (Ollama):

1. **`structure`** — detect what *kind* of audio it is (interview / monologue / lecture / news report / conversation) using cues like pauses between segments and question marks, then reformat the transcript appropriately (speaker turns, Q&A, sections).
2. **`summarize`** — a `0.0–1.0` weight controlling how hard to distill: ~0 = light cleanup/near-verbatim, ~1 = tight core-ideas-only executive summary. Tuned to keep substance, drop fluff.

I'll make them opt-in (default off, since they wake the 32B LLM), expose them both as standalone reusable endpoints (`/structure`, `/summarize`) *and* as params on `/transcribe`. The LLM calls happen **after** releasing the whisper semaphore, so they don't block other transcriptions, and they'll show up in the governor's Ollama telemetry automatically.

They require `response_format=json` (or `verbose_json`). Both methods are built and validated. Here's the summary:

## Two new post-processing methods (opt-in, LLM via Ollama)

Both run **after** the whisper semaphore releases (never block transcription), call the hub's Ollama, and the model is **per-request selectable** via `llm_model=` (default `qwen3:32b`, env `WHISPER_LLM_MODEL`).

**1. `structure`** — detects the *kind* of recording and reformats for it
- Feeds the LLM real cues: **long pauses** between segments (`>2s` gaps), **question density** (`?`-ending segments), duration, segment count — your "detect pauses / verbal questions" signals.
- Classifies as `interview` / `monologue` / `lecture` / `news_report` / `conversation`, then restructures (speaker turns, Q&A, sections) **without dropping content**.
- `structure=auto` to detect, or `structure=interview` to force a type.
- Returns `{detected_type, structured}`.

**2. `summarize`** — strength `0.0–1.0`
- ~0 = light cleanup/near-verbatim → ~0.5 = key-point bullets (~half) → ~1.0 = tight executive summary.
- Prompted to keep **substantive ideas + specifics (names/numbers), drop filler** — your "ideas not fluff."
- Returns `{summary, summary_weight}`.

**Exposed two ways** (your "two methods"):
- Inline on `/transcribe` (and `/transcribe/batch`): `-F structure=auto -F summarize=0.6` (require `response_format=json`; combinable).
- Standalone, reusable on any text you already have: `POST /structure` and `POST /summarize`.

Because they call Ollama, these LLM turns show up in the governor's telemetry automatically — no extra wiring.

So the whisper sidecar now does: **source** (file/url/path) → **transcribe** (model selectable, hot-swap) → optional **structure** + **summarize** (LLM selectable) → **output** (inline format + optional save). All compiles; routes verified.

Want me to deploy + smoke-test the whole chain now, or leave it for your `install.sh` run?

_**Agent (2026-06-04 11:59:23Z)**_

Great question — and yes, this is exactly the right instinct. Let me first answer "how does it work for an agent," then build the thing you're really asking for: a **self-describing `/agent` route** an LLM agent can hit to learn how to use the service (no human docs needed).

**How it works for an agent right now:** the agent talks pure HTTP. One model stays resident; when a request says `model=large`, the sidecar unloads turbo and loads large under a lock (the "hot-swap" you saw), then serves. `structure`/`summarize` are extra LLM passes layered on the transcript. The catch: an agent has to *know* all those params exist. A discovery endpoint fixes that — the agent fetches instructions at runtime.

Let me add `GET /agent` to the whisper sidecar — a machine-readable manifest + follow-along instructions.

_**Agent (2026-06-04 12:01:13Z)**_

The full discovery chain works. Here's the answer to both your questions:

## How it works for an agent (the short version)

Everything is plain HTTP/JSON. The agent never needs pre-baked knowledge — it **discovers** at runtime:

1. **One entry point** → `GET governor:8799/agent` returns the whole hub: the control plane (pressure, estimate, make-room) + every sidecar with a pointer to its own `/agent`.
2. **Drill in** → the agent follows `whisper → :8766/agent` and learns all 10 methods, params, 5 recipes, and step-by-step instructions.
3. **Act** → it calls `/transcribe` (picking model/format/structure/summarize), checks `/pressure` before heavy jobs, asks `/estimate` for an ETA.

The **model cache / hot-swap** an agent doesn't manage at all — it just sends `model=large` and the sidecar transparently unloads turbo, loads large under a lock, and serves. One model resident at a time; the governor watches memory so nothing has to.

## What I built

- **`GET /agent` on the whisper sidecar** — a self-describing manifest: `methods[]` (machine-readable), `input_modes`, `models` (with what's loaded *now*), `recipes`, and a follow-along `instructions` block. Reflects live runtime state.
- **`GET /agent` on the governor** — the hub-wide entry point. Lists the control plane + all four sidecars, and points to each one's `/agent` (currently only whisper implements it; the TTS ones show `null` until they get the same treatment).

So your "intro route" is real: an agent points at **`http://192.168.0.159:8799/agent`** and self-onboards to all of Atelier — no docs, no hardcoding. *(FastAPI also serves `/openapi.json` + `/docs` per sidecar, but `/agent` is the curated, task-oriented version an LLM actually wants.)*

Both compile and are live (governor + whisper restarted under launchd).

Natural next step: give the three TTS sidecars (omnivoice/kokoro/dia) the same `GET /agent` route so the hub manifest is complete — then `AGENT_CAPABLE` covers everything and an agent can fully drive TTS too. Want me to do that?

_**Agent (2026-06-04 12:37:14Z)**_

Done — the one-fetch usage is live.

## `GET /agent?expand=true` — the whole hub in one round-trip

An agent now has two modes against the **single entry point** (`:8799/agent`):

- **Default (lightweight)** → control plane + sidecar list with `agent`/`readyz` links to drill into. ~small payload.
- **`?expand=true`** → the governor **concurrently fans out** to every agent-capable sidecar's `/agent` and **inlines the full manifest** under each. One request → **12.5 KB** containing all 4 services and their 17 methods, examples, and recipes. No follow-up calls.

Verified just now:
```
omnivoice  INLINED → 2 methods
kokoro     INLINED → 3 methods
dia        INLINED → 2 methods
whisper    INLINED → 10 methods
total payload: 12461 bytes — single round-trip
```

Design details that matter:
- **Safe to expand**: `GET /agent` never wakes a model, so the fan-out adds zero memory pressure — purely reads manifests.
- **Concurrent**: `asyncio.gather` over all sidecars, 3s timeout each — fast even cold.
- **Degrades gracefully**: a down/unreachable sidecar gets an `{"unavailable": …}` stub inline instead of failing the whole response.
- **Auth-aware**: forwards the governor's `HUB_TOKEN` as a bearer when fetching (no-op here since none is set).
- **`how_to_start`** now leads with `GET /agent?expand=true` as step 1.

So the full agent story is complete: **one URL, one fetch** → an LLM agent learns the entire Atelier hub (memory state, control plane, and every TTS/ASR method with examples) and can drive it with zero hardcoded knowledge.

Everything compiles and the governor's running under launchd with the change. That rounds out the whole arc — whisper sidecar built, smoke-tested, local-model-pinned, dashboard-wired, and the hub made fully agent-discoverable.

Opt-in per request.\nNORMALIZE_FILTERS = {\n    # EBU R128 broadcast loudness — consistent target level, great default.\n    \"loudnorm\": \"loudnorm=I=-16:TP=-1.5:LRA=11\",\n    # Dynamic normalizer — lifts quiet passages, smooths level swings.\n    \"dynaudnorm\": \"dynaudnorm=f=150:g=15\",\n    # ffmpeg's purpose-built speech leveler.\n    \"speechnorm\": \"speechnorm=e=12.5:r=0.0001:l=1\",\n    # Speech cleanup chain: cut low rumble -> dynamic-normalize -> peak-limit.\n    \"speech\": \"highpass=f=80,dynaudnorm=f=150:g=15,alimiter=limit=0.95\",\n}\n\n\ndef _ffmpeg_preprocess(in_path: str, normalize: str | None, gain_db: float | None) -> tuple[str, bool]:\n    \"\"\"Apply optional gain + a normalization filter via ffmpeg, writing a 16 kHz\n    mono wav (whisper's native input). Returns (path, is_temp). No-op (returns the\n    input untouched) when neither is requested.\"\"\"\n    filters: list[str] = []\n    if gain_db:\n        filters.append(f\"volume={gain_db}dB\")\n    if normalize:\n        mode = \"speech\" if normalize.strip().lower() in (\"true\", \"1\", \"yes\", \"auto\") else normalize.strip().lower()\n        flt = NORMALIZE_FILTERS.get(mode)\n        if flt is None:\n            raise HTTPException(400, f\"unknown normalize mode '{normalize}'; choose one of \"\n                                     f\"{sorted(NORMALIZE_FILTERS)} or true/auto\")\n        filters.append(flt)\n    if not filters:\n        return in_path, False\n    fd, out = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=\"whisper-norm-\", suffix=\".wav\")\n    os.close(fd)\n    cmd = [\"ffmpeg\", \"-y\", \"-i\", in_path, \"-af\", \",\".join(filters),\n           \"-ar\", \"16000\", \"-ac\", \"1\", out]\n    proc = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True)\n    if proc.returncode != 0:\n        try:\n            os.unlink(out)\n        except OSError:\n            pass\n        raise HTTPException(500, f\"ffmpeg preprocess failed: {proc.stderr.decode(errors='replace')[-300:]}\")\n    return out, True\n\n\n# ---------- transcript formatting + output ----------\ndef _ts(seconds: float, sep: str) -> str:"}

Honest result worth noting: I made the clip **extremely** quiet (−66.5 dB, way below the −42.5 dB original) and **whisper still nailed it without normalization** — because whisper internally normalizes its mel-spectrogram, so it's quite robust to pure quietness. Let me answer your question directly and document it.

## Yes — and it's now wired in

ffmpeg has all the right tools, and the whisper sidecar now exposes them as opt-in preprocessing on `/transcribe` (and batch):

| `normalize=` | ffmpeg filter | best for |
|---|---|---|
| `loudnorm` | EBU R128 `loudnorm=I=-16:TP=-1.5:LRA=11` | consistent broadcast loudness |
| `dynaudnorm` | `dynaudnorm` | lifting quiet passages, smoothing swings |
| `speechnorm` | `speechnorm` | ffmpeg's purpose-built speech leveler |
| `speech` (or `true`) | `highpass=80, dynaudnorm, alimiter` | **default** — rumble-cut → level → peak-limit |
| `gain_db=N` | `volume=NdB` | fixed boost (stacks before normalize) |

It writes a 16 kHz mono temp wav (whisper's native input), runs **before** the model on the CPU (not holding the GPU lock), and the **cache key stays the sha256 of the *original* audio** so normalization doesn't fork your cache.

_**Agent (2026-06-04 17:03:59Z)**_

Done. Direct answer to your question, then what shipped:

## Yes — ffmpeg has all of it
- **Loudness normalization**: `loudnorm` (EBU R128, the broadcast standard) and `dynaudnorm` (dynamic — lifts quiet parts)
- **Speech leveler**: `speechnorm` (purpose-built for exactly this)
- **Limiter**: `alimiter` (lookahead peak limiter — prevents the boost from clipping)
- **Compressor / gain**: `acompressor`, `volume`

## What I wired into the whisper sidecar
- New `normalize=` param (`loudnorm` | `dynaudnorm` | `speechnorm` | `speech` | `true`) and `gain_db=` on `/transcribe` and `/transcribe/batch`.
- The `speech` preset (default for `normalize=true`) is a proper cleanup chain: **high-pass 80 Hz (cut rumble) → dynaudnorm (level) → alimiter (prevent clipping)**.
- Runs via ffmpeg → 16 kHz mono temp wav, **before** the model, on the CPU (doesn't hold the GPU lock). Temp files cleaned up. Cache key unchanged (original audio's sha256).
- Surfaced in the `/agent` manifest (params + a "quiet/uneven recording" recipe) and the README.

## Verified
Made a clip 24 dB quieter (−66.5 dB) and ran it three ways — all transcribed correctly; normalization even fixed a tiny error ("Sand Walk" → "sandwalk"). The honest takeaway: **whisper is already robust to pure quietness** (internal mel normalization), so on clean-but-quiet audio the gain is modest. The real payoff is **degraded real-world audio** — uneven speaker levels, background rumble, AGC artifacts — where leveling meaningfully improves the transcript. It's there when you need it, off by default.

Compiles and live under launchd. Want me to also expose this as a knob the TTS side could reuse (a shared `/normalize` utility), or leave it whisper-local?

normalize/gain/model\".\n# Thresholds follow whisper-community norms (avg_logprob<-1.0, no_speech>0.6,\n# compression_ratio>2.4 ≈ repetition/hallucination).\ndef _suggest(low: bool, normalized: bool, gained: bool) -> str | None:\n    if not low:\n        return None\n    if not normalized:\n        return \"low confidence — retry with normalize=speech (add gain_db=6 if the audio is very faint)\"\n    if not gained:\n        return \"still low after normalize — retry adding gain_db=6, or model=large for higher accuracy\"\n    return \"still low after normalize+gain — try model=large, or the audio may be too degraded / non-speech\"\n\n\ndef _quality(result: dict, *, normalized: bool, gained: bool) -> dict:\n    segs = result.get(\"segments\", [])\n    if not segs:\n        return {\"low_confidence\": True, \"confidence\": 0.0, \"segments\": 0,\n                \"reasons\": [\"no speech segments returned\"],\n                \"avg_logprob\": None, \"min_logprob\": None,\n                \"max_no_speech_prob\": None, \"max_compression_ratio\": None,\n                \"suggestion\": _suggest(True, normalized, gained)}\n    logs = [s[\"avg_logprob\"] for s in segs if s.get(\"avg_logprob\") is not None]\n    nsp = [s[\"no_speech_prob\"] for s in segs if s.get(\"no_speech_prob\") is not None]\n    crs = [s[\"compression_ratio\"] for s in segs if s.get(\"compression_ratio\") is not None]\n    avg_logprob = round(statistics.mean(logs), 3) if logs else None\n    min_logprob = round(min(logs), 3) if logs else None\n    max_nsp = round(max(nsp), 3) if nsp else None\n    max_cr = round(max(crs), 3) if crs else None\n    reasons = []\n    if avg_logprob is not None and avg_logprob < -1.0:\n        reasons.append(f\"low avg_logprob compression_ratio {max_cr} (possible repetition/hallucination)\")\n    low = bool(reasons)\n    return {\n        \"low_confidence\": low,\n        # avg_logprob → 0..1 proxy (exp): ~-0.1 good ≈0.90, ~-1.0 weak ≈0.37.\n        \"confidence\": round(math.exp(avg_logprob), 3) if avg_logprob is not None else None,\n        \"avg_logprob\": avg_logprob, \"min_logprob\": min_logprob,\n }\n\n\n# ---------- HTTP: health ----------\n@app.get(\"/healthz\")\ndef healthz():"}

_**Agent (2026-06-04 17:38:12Z)**_

Done. The agent now has the exact signal you described — a quality readout in every transcription response that tells it when the transcript is bad and which parameter to set.

## What ships

**Every json `/transcribe` response now includes a `quality` block:**
```json
"quality": {
  "low_confidence": true/false,
  "confidence": 0.0–1.0,            // proxy from avg_logprob
  "avg_logprob", "max_no_speech_prob", "max_compression_ratio",
  "text_density_cps", "audio_seconds", "segments",
  "reasons": [...],
  "suggestion": "retry with normalize=speech ..."   // ← the param to set
}
```
Plus `x-asr-confidence` / `x-asr-low-confidence` headers for `text`/`srt`/`vtt` callers.

**`low_confidence` trips on any of** (whisper-community thresholds):
- `avg_logprob < -1.0` (low model confidence)
- `no_speech_prob > 0.6` (likely silence/noise)
- `compression_ratio > 2.4` (repetition/hallucination)
- **low text density** — the heuristic I added after the first test, which catches the classic **"Thank you." hallucination** on near-silent audio that logprob alone misses

**The `suggestion` field drives an explicit escalation ladder** an agent just follows:
```
transcribe → low_confidence? → normalize=speech → still? → +gain_db=6 → still? → model=large
```
Each step is the same audio with the one parameter named in `suggestion`; it stops when confidence clears or after `model=large`.

## Verified
- Clean clip → `low_confidence: false`, confidence 0.85, density 14.4 cps
- Degraded clip → `low_confidence: true`, density 0.67 cps, reason logged, suggestion = `normalize=speech`

Wired into the `/agent` manifest too (`quality_signal` block + a "self-correct" recipe), so an agent discovers the loop at runtime. Compiles, live under launchd, README documents it.

So the full ASR story is now self-driving: an agent transcribes, reads `quality`, and if it's bad, re-runs with the suggested `normalize`/`gain_db`/`model` — no human in the loop. Anything else on this, or shall I leave it here?

Short answer: **No — everything you've built is already live. No restart or reinstall needed right now.**

I restarted each service as I changed it, so the current state is:

| Component | Status | Why |
|---|---|---|
| whisper `:8766` | ✅ **latest code running** (verified: `text_density_cps` present) | I `kickstart`ed it after the quality change |

## The rules going forward

**Restart (`launchctl kickstart -k …`) — not reinstall — when you edit a sidecar's `server.py`.** The service code is *symlinked* from the repo into `~/services/`, so the file is always current; the running Python process just needs to reload. That's a 2-second restart:
```sh
launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/io.macstudio.hub.whisper
```

**Reinstall (`deploy/install.sh`) only for:**
- New/changed **dependencies** (a `requirements.txt` edit) — needs `uv pip install` in the venv
- A **brand-new sidecar** or a **new launchd plist**
- A **fresh machine**

I already did the equivalent of the install for whisper by hand during the smoke test (venv + deps + plist bootstrap), and `install.sh` is updated so a future fresh install includes whisper automatically — so **no reinstall is pending**.

## One thing that *does* need a rebuild (when you want it)

The **dashboard's Rust changes** (the `get_sidecars` whisper fetch + the `asr_rtf` log parser) only go live after a `cargo tauri build` (or running it in dev). The dashboard *frontend* changes (whisper card, mem estimate, mocks) load from disk on the next refresh. The sidecar/governor work needs none of that.

So: nothing to do unless you edit a sidecar again (→ kickstart) or want the dashboard app rebuilt (→ I can run that for you). Want me to rebuild the dashboard so its Rust side picks up the whisper wiring?

_**Agent (2026-06-04 20:01:51Z)**_

I found the real reason, and it's a **bug worth fixing** — not just a label.

## First, your actual question: yes, whisper is fully in the memory system ✅

- **Its own job-aware idle-watcher**: `/readyz` shows `idle_unload_seconds: 300`, `keep_warm: false`, and it tracks `active_jobs`/`queue_depth` — it will **not** unload mid-transcription.
- **Governor make-room** includes it: the dry-run returned `would_evict: ['kokoro', 'whisper']` (both warm+idle). It only evicts `lifecycle == "idle"`, and whisper's `/admin/unload` refuses while busy — job-aware at **two** layers.
- **Force-stop** accepts `target=whisper` (validated against `SIDECAR_BASE`).

So whisper behaves exactly like the other sidecars.

## Why qwen shows "busy" — two reasons, one is a bug

**1. Labeling:** the governor marks *any resident* Ollama model "busy" (Ollama's only signal is `expires_at`/keep-alive, no in-flight flag). So a merely-loaded model reads "busy."

**2. The real problem — a self-feedback loop.** qwen3:32b is genuinely being hit ~**1 `/api/generate` per second**, and the caller is **the governor itself**. Its `_ollama_stats_watcher` (line 414) works like this:
```
real call completes → watcher fires a tiny 8-token probe to measure tok/s (keep_alive=5m)
   → that probe is ALSO logged as an /api/generate call
   → 0.5s later the watcher sees "a new call completed!" → fires another probe
   → … forever
```
My earlier `structure`/`summarize` tests made the first real qwen call, which **seeded the loop** — and it's been self-sustaining since. The effect: **qwen3:32b (31 GB) is pinned resident**, keep-alive refreshed every second, GPU doing endless 8-token gens. That directly defeats the memory governor.

## The fix
The watcher must not treat its **own** probe as a triggering call. Two-line guard:
- a **cooldown** (e.g. probe at most once per ~30s), which alone breaks the runaway, and
- after probing, advance `last_call_ts` past the probe's own log entry so it can't re-trigger.

That keeps the fresh-stats feature but stops the loop. I can also immediately stop the bleeding (evict qwen via `/make-room`, restart the governor) so it releases the 31 GB now.

Want me to apply the watcher fix and clear qwen out? It's a real bug in the governor that's burning memory + compute continuously.

_**Agent (2026-06-04 20:06:10Z)**_

Fixed and cleared. Final state is clean:

## Result
- **Memory freed**: `free_gb` 17.6 → **49.2 GB**, pressure level `warn` → **`ok`**
- **qwen evicted**: Ollama shows no models loaded; no ollama tenant in `/pressure`
- **Loop dead**: 0 `/api/generate` calls over 25s and again over 8s (was ~1/sec)
- **All sidecars idle/cold**, nothing pinned — the hub is genuinely at rest now

## What I changed
**The bug** (`_ollama_stats_watcher`): its measurement probe was itself an `/api/generate` call, which got logged → the watcher saw "a new call!" → fired another probe → forever, pinning qwen3:32b (31 GB) resident and burning GPU.

**The fix** (`sidecars/governor/server.py`):
1. **Cooldown** — `PROBE_COOLDOWN` (60s, env-tunable): at most one probe per window, so it physically can't run away.
2. **Self-consume** — after probing, advance `last_call_ts` past every logged call (including the probe's own), so the probe can't re-trigger the watcher.

The fresh-tok/s-stats feature still works (it probes once after real activity); it just can't loop.

## Cleanup note
The reason my first restart didn't take: a **stale governor instance was lingering** (didn't die on `kickstart`, so the new one couldn't bind `:8799`). I booted out the launchd job, hard-killed the strays, and re-bootstrapped — now there's a single clean governor (the fix is confirmed live by the 0-call result).

The fix is in the repo (symlinked → already running). One thing to know: the loop only *seeds* when something makes a real LLM call — so my earlier `structure`/`summarize` tests kicked it off. With the fix, that can't escalate anymore. Whisper, for the record, was never involved — it's fully and correctly wired into the memory governor, which is what you originally asked.

_**Agent (2026-06-04 22:30:27Z)**_

That confirms it. Here's the honest picture:

## The per-sidecar memory is an **estimate**, not measured

The governor's `poll_sidecar` only returns `state`, `active_jobs`, `queue_depth` — **no memory**. The dashboard then fills in `mem` from a hardcoded lookup table (`SIDECAR_MEM = {whisper: 2.0, kokoro: 4.0, dia: 8.0, …}`), shown whenever the sidecar isn't cold.

**Ollama tenants are different** — they carry *real* `mem_gb` from `/api/ps`. Only the **atelier sidecars** use the static guess.

And the guesses are off, especially when idle. Real RSS right now vs. the estimate:

| sidecar | dashboard estimate | actual RSS | |
|---|---|---|---|
| whisper | 2.0 GB | **2.34 GB** | warm/loaded — close |
| kokoro | 4.0 GB | **0.10 GB** | cold — estimate 40× too high |
| dia | 8.0 GB | **0.67 GB** | cold |
| omnivoice | 12.0 GB | **0.51 GB** | cold |

So when a sidecar finishes a job and unloads, the dashboard keeps showing the loaded-model estimate until it goes fully cold — it does **not** reflect actual active memory.

## The fix (and it's clean)
Have each sidecar report its **own real RSS** in `/readyz` (one cheap `ps -o rss= -p <pid>` call, no new dependency), then the governor passes that through as `mem_gb`. The dashboard already prefers a real value (`t.mem_gb ?? SIDECAR_MEM[...]`), so **the frontend needs zero changes** — real numbers just start flowing, and `SIDECAR_MEM` becomes a fallback for when a sidecar is unreachable.

That makes the memory column track actual usage live: ~2.3 GB when whisper is transcribing, ~0.1 GB when it's idle-unloaded.

It touches the 4 sidecars + the governor's `poll_sidecar`. Want me to wire it in?

Verified now — here's the real picture. **Gemini fabricated** "Rapid-MLX", "oMLX", and "SwiftLM" (and that brew tap). None appear in any search. Here are the **actual, verified** Apple Silicon serving options:

## MLX-native LLM servers (the "mx library for Mac" you meant)

| Project | What it is | Launch | Models |
|---|---|---|---|
| **mlx-lm** (Apple official) | The canonical MLX LLM server, OpenAI-compatible `/v1` | `mlx_lm.server --model mlx-community/<m> --port 8080` | `mlx-community` safetensors |
| **FastMLX** (Blaizzy) | Production server, **multi-model dynamic load/unload**, VLM + tool calling | `fastmlx` (then POST model name) | MLX safetensors |
| **vllm-mlx** (waybarrios) | OpenAI **+ Anthropic** API, continuous batching, MCP tool calling, "400+ tok/s", works with Claude Code | server CLI | MLX |
| **mlx-openai-server** (cubist38) | OpenAI-compatible, vision + language | CLI | MLX |

## The llama.cpp / Metal route (GGUF)
- **`llama-server`** — run llama.cpp's own server directly (Metal backend, OpenAI `/v1`, GGUF). `brew install llama.cpp` → `llama-server -m model.gguf --port 8081 -ngl 99`. You already get llama.cpp *through* Ollama; a direct `llama-server` sidecar just gives finer control (KV-cache quant, router mode). 
- **MLC-LLM** (`mlc_llm serve`) — Metal/TVM, fast but needs a per-model compile step (less convenient).
- **llamafile** — single-file Metal server; handy for portability, not for a managed hub.

## My recommendation for Atelier
Since you already run **MLX for whisper + mflux** and pull from `mlx-community`, the cleanest native LLM sidecar is **mlx-lm** (`mlx_lm.server`) — Apple-official, same model ecosystem, OpenAI-compatible, drops straight into your sidecar pattern. If you want **multiple models with on-the-fly load/unload** (which pairs nicely with your memory governor), **FastMLX** is the better fit. Both are real and maintained; either complements Ollama (faster on Apple Silicon) without replacing it.

It would slot in on a free hub port (8767 is mflux, 8768 is the reserved slot), register with the governor, and honor idle-unload — FastMLX natively, mlx-lm via a thin wrapper.

Cold-starts the\n    child if needed, streams the response (stream=true SSE works), and tracks\n    in-flight requests so idle-unload can't kill a live generation.\"\"\"\n    global _active, _last_request_at\n    _check_auth(request)\n    await _ensure_started()\n    body = await request.body()\n    headers = {k: v for k, v in request.headers.items()\n               if k.lower() not in (\"host\", \"content-length\", \"authorization\")}\n    url = f\"{CHILD_BASE}/v1/{path}\"\n    client = httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=None)\n    _active += 1\n    try:\n        req = client.build_request(request.method, url, headers=headers,\n                                   content=body, params=request.query_params)\n        resp = await client.send(req, stream=True)\n    except Exception as e:\n        _active -= 1\n        _last_request_at = time.monotonic()\n        await client.aclose()\n        raise HTTPException(502, f\"engine proxy failed: {e}\")\n\n    async def streamer():\n        global _active, _last_request_at\n        try:\n            async for chunk in resp.aiter_raw():\n                yield chunk\n        finally:\n            await resp.aclose()\n            await client.aclose()\n            _active -= 1\n            _last_request_at = time.monotonic()\n\n    passthru = {k: v for k, v in resp.headers.items()\n                if k.lower() not in (\"content-length\", \"transfer-encoding\", \"connection\")}\n    return StreamingResponse(streamer(), status_code=resp.status_code,\n                             headers=passthru, media_type=resp.headers.get(\"content-type\"))\n"}

```json
{"file_path":"/Users/gyasisutton/Documents/code/atelier/sidecars/llamacpp/README.md","content":"# llamacpp-sidecar — LLM via llama.cpp (Metal, GGUF)\n\nA thin **managed wrapper** around llama.cpp's `llama-server`. Port **8771**. Part of the Mac Studio inference hub.\n\n`llama-server` already speaks the OpenAI API and Metal-accelerates GGUF models — this wrapper subprocess-manages it on an internal port, proxies `/v1/*`, and adds the Atelier contract (`/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/admin/unload`, `/agent`, **idle-unload**) so the governor can monitor and idle-evict it like every other sidecar.\n\n```\nclient → :8771/v1/chat/completions      (Atelier-fronted OpenAI API)\n         :8771/healthz /readyz /agent /admin/unload\n         └─ proxies → 127.0.0.1:18771    (llama-server child, Metal/GGUF)\nidle → wrapper stops the child → model memory freed.\n```\n\n## Install / deploy\n\nThe wrapper needs only FastAPI + httpx (in `requirements.txt`); the **engine installs separately**:\n\n```sh\nbrew install llama.cpp          # provides `llama-server`\n# put a GGUF model at ~/models/gguf/ and point LLAMACPP_MODEL at it\n```\n\n`deploy/install.sh` creates the venv, symlinks `server.py`, and drops the launchd plist. Edit the plist's `LLAMACPP_MODEL` to your `.gguf`.\n\n## Use (OpenAI-compatible)\n\n```sh\ncurl -s http://192.168.0.159:8771/v1/chat/completions -H 'content-type: application/json' \\\n  -d '{\"model\":\"<alias>\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hello\"}]}'\n\n# streaming\ncurl -sN http://192.168.0.159:8771/v1/chat/completions -H 'content-type: application/json' \\\n  -d '{\"model\":\"<alias>\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hi\"}],\"stream\":true}'\n```\n\nPoint any OpenAI client at base URL `http://192.168.0.159:8771/v1` (api_key = your `HUB_TOKEN`, or anything if unset).\n\n## Lifecycle\n\n| Endpoint | Purpose |\n|---|---|\n| `GET /healthz` | liveness (wrapper only — never starts the engine) |\n| `GET /readyz` | warm/cold/busy, child pid, model, idle seconds |\n| `GET /agent` | machine-readable manifest for agents |\n| `POST /admin/unload[?force=true]` | stop the engine to free memory |\n| `ANY /v1/{path}` | OpenAI proxy (cold-starts the engine on first call) |\n\nThe engine **cold-starts on the first `/v1` call** and **idle-unloads** after `IDLE_UNLOAD_SECONDS` (default 600) so a forgotten chat model doesn't squat 8–30 GB. `KEEP_WARM=true` for an always-hot assistant. In-flight requests are tracked so idle-unload never kills a live generation.\n\n## Env vars\n\n| Var | Default |\n|---|---|\n| `LLAMACPP_BIN` | `llama-server` (PATH / Homebrew) |\n| `LLAMACPP_MODEL` | — (required: path to a `.gguf`) |\n| `LLAMACPP_ALIAS` | model file stem (name reported to clients) |\n| `LLAMACPP_PORT` | `8771` (public) |\n| `LLAMACPP_CHILD_PORT` | `18771` (internal `llama-server`) |\n| `LLAMACPP_ARGS` | extra args, e.g. `--ctx-size 8192 -ngl 99 --flash-attn` |\n| `IDLE_UNLOAD_SECONDS` | `600` |\n| `KEEP_WARM` | `false` |\n| `HUB_TOKEN` | unset |\n\n> GGUF/Metal path. For MLX-native models use the **fastmlx** sidecar (`:8772`). Both complement Ollama, which also wraps llama.cpp but with less control.\n"}
```

the model loads on demand.\n\n## Install / deploy\n\n```sh\n# the engine + MLX come in via requirements.txt (fastmlx, mlx, mlx-lm, mlx-vlm)\n# Apple Silicon only.\n```\n\n`deploy/install.sh` creates the venv, installs `requirements.txt` (which provides the `fastmlx` CLI), symlinks `server.py`, and drops the launchd plist.\n\n## Use (OpenAI-compatible)\n\n```sh\ncurl -s http://192.168.0.159:8772/v1/chat/completions -H 'content-type: application/json' \\\n  -d '{\"model\":\"mlx-community/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-4bit\",\n       \"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hello\"}]}'\n\n# pre-load a model (else it loads on first chat call)\ncurl -s -X POST \"http://192.168.0.159:8772/v1/models?model_name=mlx-community/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-4bit\"\n```\n\nSet `model` to any `mlx-community` repo. `stream:true` for SSE; `tools:[…]` for tool calling; image content for VLMs. Point any OpenAI client at `http://192.168.0.159:8772/v1`.\n\n## Lifecycle\n\n| Endpoint | Purpose |\n|---|---|\n| `GET /healthz` | liveness (wrapper only) |\n| `GET /readyz` | warm/cold/busy, child pid, idle seconds |\n| `GET /agent` | machine-readable manifest for agents |\n| `POST /admin/unload[?force=true]` | stop the engine to free MLX memory |\n| `ANY /v1/{path}` | OpenAI proxy (cold-starts the engine on first call) |\n\nEngine **cold-starts on first `/v1` call**, **idle-unloads** after `IDLE_UNLOAD_SECONDS` (default 600). In-flight requests are tracked so idle-unload can't interrupt a live generation.\n\n## Env vars\n\n| Var | Default |\n|---|---|\n| `FASTMLX_BIN` | `fastmlx` (venv CLI) |\n| `FASTMLX_PORT` | `8772` (public) |\n| `FASTMLX_CHILD_PORT` | `18772` (internal FastMLX) |\n| `FASTMLX_DEFAULT_MODEL` | informational, for `/agent` |\n| `FASTMLX_ARGS` | extra args, e.g. `--workers 1` |\n| `IDLE_UNLOAD_SECONDS` | `600` |\n| `KEEP_WARM` | `false` |\n| `HUB_TOKEN` | unset |\n\n> MLX-native path. For GGUF models use the **llamacpp** sidecar (`:8771`).\n"}

Port **8765**. The hub's **fastest** speech engine (~sub-second per line) — the low-latency fallback when you don't need cloning or expressive prosody.\n\n## Use\n\n```sh\ncurl -s http://192.168.0.159:8765/voices                         # list voice ids\ncurl -s http://192.168.0.159:8765/tts -H 'content-type: application/json' \\\n  -d '{\"text\":\"Hello there\",\"voice\":\"af_bella\",\"speed\":1.0}' --output out.wav\n```\n\n## Endpoints\n\n| Endpoint | Purpose |\n|---|---|\n| `GET /healthz` · `GET /readyz` | liveness / warm-cold-busy + queue depth |\n| `GET /voices` | available voice ids + default |\n| `GET /agent` | machine-readable manifest for agents |\n| `POST /tts` | `{text, voice, speed, lang}` → `audio/wav` |\n| `POST /admin/unload[?force=true]` | drop the model to free memory |\n\nSingle-flight (`asyncio.Semaphore(1)` — CoreML EP is single-stream). Defaults to `KEEP_WARM=true` (serves the live podcast pipeline); set `KEEP_WARM=false` to idle-unload.\n\n## Model & env\n\n- `Kokoro-82M-v1.0-ONNX` q8 (~325 MB) at `~/models/kokoro/` (`kokoro-v1.0.fp16.onnx` + `voices-v1.0.bin`).\n- `KOKORO_MODEL_PATH`, `KOKORO_VOICES_PATH`, `KOKORO_DEFAULT_VOICE` (default `am_michael`), `IDLE_UNLOAD_SECONDS`, `KEEP_WARM`, `HUB_TOKEN`.\n\n> Need expressive/cloned voices → **dia** (`:8769`). Need instruct-driven accents → **omnivoice** (`:8770`).\n"}

Auto-detects device (cuda/mps/cpu).\n\n## Model & env\n\n- `k2-fsa/OmniVoice` (auto-downloads via `HF_HOME` on first start).\n- `OMNIVOICE_MODEL`, `OMNIVOICE_DEVICE`, `IDLE_UNLOAD_SECONDS`, `KEEP_WARM`, `HUB_TOKEN`.\n\n> Fastest fixed voices → **kokoro** (`:8765`). Expressive `[S1]/[S2]` dialogue cloning → **dia** (`:8769`).\n"}

```json
{"file_path":"/Users/gyasisutton/Documents/code/atelier/sidecars/governor/README.md","content":"# governor-sidecar — hub supervisor\n\nThe Atelier hub's brain. Port **8799**. Watches unified-memory pressure across Ollama + all sidecars, evicts **idle** models to make room, records every run, and predicts ETAs. It's the single entry point for agents (`/agent`) and the dashboard's main data source.\n\n## What it does\n\n- **Memory governor** — polls `/api/ps` (Ollama) + each sidecar's `/readyz`, computes a pressure level, and on ALARM auto-runs idle eviction. Preempting a *busy* model is human-gated.\n- **Telemetry** — tails the Ollama log + sidecar logs (`[tts]`, `[asr]`) into one observable pane.\n- **Predictor** — Bayesian per-(kind, model) ETA estimator (`predictor.py`, persistent SQLite at `~/.atelier/predictor.db`).\n\n## Endpoints\n\n| Endpoint | Purpose |\n|---|---|\n| `GET /agent[?expand=true]` | **hub manifest** — control plane + every sidecar (inline with `expand`) |\n| `GET /pressure` | `{level, free_gb, resident_gb, tenants[], alerts, recommendation}` |\n| `GET /telemetry` | recent calls, synths, events, live Ollama perf |\n| `GET /estimate` | predicted ETA — `?engine=whisper&audio_s=N` / `?engine=<tts>&chars=N` / `?model=<llm>&out_tokens=N` |\n| `GET /predictor/stats` · `/predictor/export` | learned compute stats / portable dataset |\n| `GET /benchmark?model=<m>` | fire a real generate, measure decode tok/s, record it |\n| `POST /report` | feed a completed run into the predictor |\n| `POST /make-room` | evict ONLY idle models (safe, agent-callable) |\n| `POST /force-stop` | two-phase, human-gated preempt of a BUSY model |\n\n## Registry\n\nNew sidecars are added to the dicts near the top of `server.py`: `SIDECAR_BASE` (port), `SIDECAR_LABELS` (launchd label, for force-stop), `SIDECAR_ROLES` + `AGENT_CAPABLE` (hub manifest). Monitoring, idle-eviction, and `/agent` discovery then include them automatically.\n\n## Env\n\n`ATELIER_POLL_SECONDS` (10), `OLLAMA_URL`, `OLLAMA_LOG`, `ATELIER_AUTO_MAKE_ROOM` (1), `ATELIER_AUTO_COOLDOWN` (60), `ATELIER_PROBE_COOLDOWN` (60), `HUB_TOKEN`.\n"}
```

_**Agent (2026-06-05 07:37:41Z)**_

Done — both LLM serving sidecars are scaffolded as full managed wrappers, and **every sidecar now has documentation**.

## Two new managed-wrapper sidecars

| Sidecar | Port | Engine | What it adds |
|---|---|---|---|
| **llamacpp** | 8771 (child 18771) | llama.cpp `llama-server` (Metal, GGUF) | OpenAI `/v1` proxy + Atelier contract |
| **fastmlx** | 8772 (child 18772) | FastMLX (MLX-native) | OpenAI `/v1` proxy + Atelier contract |

Each wrapper **subprocess-manages** its engine on an internal port and proxies `/v1/*` (streaming SSE included), while adding the full hub contract: `/healthz`, `/readyz` (lifecycle), `/admin/unload`, **`/agent`**, and **idle-unload** that stops the child to free 8–30 GB. In-flight requests are tracked so idle-unload can't kill a live generation — exactly like kokoro/whisper.

**Collision-safe & opt-out friendly** (your requirement): each has its own port, plist, and venv. The governor handles any sidecar being absent (shows `unreachable`), so you can run or skip either one independently — no port clashes (8771/8772 public, 18771/18772 internal, all outside the existing 8765–8770/8799 set).

## Documentation
- **READMEs written for all 7 sidecars** — the two new ones plus the previously-undocumented kokoro, dia, omnivoice, and governor. Each has purpose, port, curl examples, endpoints, env vars.
- Both new sidecars expose `/agent`; the **hub manifest now lists all six** workload sidecars (confirmed live).
- Wired into: governor (`SIDECAR_BASE`/`LABELS`/`ROLES`/`AGENT_CAPABLE`), `install.sh` (venv loop + `brew install llama.cpp` note + `gguf` dir + verify ports), `doctor.sh` port registry, dashboard (`get_sidecars`, `SIDECAR_MEM`, mocks), and the hub docs (ATELIER.md + ARCHITECTURE port map).
- Removed the stray `_gpu_mem_gb` helper from the earlier misread task.

## What's scaffolded vs. live
This is **scaffold only** — code, docs, plists, and registration are in the repo, and the governor already advertises both. To go live you'd run `install.sh` (or per-sidecar: `brew install llama.cpp` + a GGUF for llamacpp; `pip install fastmlx` via the venv for fastmlx), set the model env in each plist, and `launchctl bootstrap`. Everything compiles/validates (Python, JS, plists, bash).

## How to use it (OpenAI-compatible, on the LAN)
```sh
curl -s http://192.168.0.159:8771/v1/chat/completions -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gemma4-12b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"..."}],
       "chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":false}}'
```
Point any OpenAI client at base URL `http://192.168.0.159:8771/v1`, model `gemma4-12b`.

## Important note about gemma4:12b
It's a **reasoning/thinking model** (llama.cpp: `Chat format: peg-gemma4, thinking=1`). Output splits into `reasoning_content` (chain-of-thought) and `content` (answer). So:
- For **one-shot answers**, pass `"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":false}` → clean direct reply (verified).
- Otherwise give a **generous `max_tokens`** — it spends the budget thinking first, and a small limit leaves `content` empty with `finish_reason: length`.

It cold-starts on first call (~3s model load) and idle-unloads after 10 min idle so it doesn't squat ~7.4 GB.

_**Agent (2026-06-06 10:22:02Z)**_

That's the deal-breaker: **`TypeError: generate_step() got an unexpected keyword argument 'temp'`**. Patching the imports got FastMLX to load, but its **generation code also uses removed mlx-lm APIs** — mlx-lm replaced `generate_step(temp=…)` with a new sampler API. Fixing this means rewriting FastMLX's core generation logic in several places (and likely more breakage after) — that's **forking and maintaining FastMLX**, not a patch. Not worth it.

Here's the honest scorecard:

**What's proven working** (my wrapper is validated):
- ✅ Wrapper lifecycle: `/readyz` cold→warm→cold, `/admin/unload`, child cold-start on MPS
- ✅ Model add through the proxy ("added successfully")
- ✅ The OpenAI proxy plumbing itself
- ❌ FastMLX's actual text generation — incompatible with mlx-lm 0.31.3 internals

**The root cause is FastMLX, not the sidecar.** FastMLX 0.2.1 (latest + git main) is effectively unmaintained against current mlx-lm.

## Recommendation: swap the engine to `mlx_lm.server`
Apple's official MLX server tracks mlx-lm exactly, is OpenAI-compatible, and I **already verified mlx-lm loads + generates from your local model** (`Hello, how may I assist you?` in 0.3s). My wrapper needs only a small change — the child spawn becomes `python -m mlx_lm server --model <dir>` (one model at startup, like llamacpp). Everything else (proxy, lifecycle, idle-unload, `/agent`, governor) stays. Low-risk, and it'll actually generate.

I'd keep the `fastmlx` scaffold in the repo (documented as "blocked on upstream — re-enable when FastMLX catches up to mlx-lm") and stand up an **`mlxlm` sidecar** wrapping `mlx_lm.server` as the working MLX-native LLM path.

Want me to do that now — wire the `mlxlm` sidecar (reusing the proven wrapper) and smoke-test it with the Qwen2.5-0.5B model I already downloaded? Then you'd have **two working LLM sidecars**: llamacpp (GGUF/gemma4:12b) + mlxlm (MLX-native).
