stream=true supported)\",\n             \"params\": \"{model, messages[], temperature, max_tokens, stream, …}\",\n             \"returns\": \"OpenAI chat completion (or SSE stream)\",\n             \"example\": \"curl -s $URL/v1/chat/completions -H 'content-type: application/json' \"\n                        f\"-d '{{\\\"model\\\":\\\"{ALIAS}\\\",\\\"messages\\\":[{{\\\"role\\\":\\\"user\\\",\\\"content\\\":\\\"hi\\\"}}]}}'\"},\n            {\"name\": \"completions\", \"http\": \"POST /v1/completions\", \"returns\": \"OpenAI text completion\"},\n            {\"name\": \"models\", \"http\": \"GET /v1/models\", \"returns\": \"served model list\"},\n            {\"name\": \"readyz\", \"http\": \"GET /readyz\", \"returns\": \"warm/cold/busy + child pid\"},\n            {\"name\": \"unload\", \"http\": \"POST /admin/unload\", \"returns\": \"stops the engine to free memory\"},\n        ],\n        \"recipes\": [\n            {\"goal\": \"MLX-native OpenAI chat\", \"do\": \"POST /v1/chat/completions with your messages\"},\n            {\"goal\": \"Free the memory now\", \"do\": \"POST /admin/unload\"},\n        ],\n        \"instructions\": (\n            \"1) POST /v1/chat/completions like the OpenAI API (stream=true for SSE).\\n\"\n            \"2) The engine cold-starts on the first call (model load takes seconds) and \"\n            \"idle-unloads after inactivity.\\n\"\n            \"3) GET /readyz for warm/cold; POST /admin/unload to free memory.\\n\"\n            \"4) This is the MLX-native path; for GGUF models use the llamacpp sidecar.\"\n        ),\n        \"openapi\": \"/openapi.json\",\n    }\n\n\n@app.get(\"/models\")\nasync def models(request: Request):\n    _check_auth(request)\n    await _ensure_started()\n    async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:\n        try:\n            r = await client.get(f\"{CHILD_BASE}/v1/models\", timeout=5)\n            return r.json()\n        except Exception as e:\n            raise HTTPException(502, f\"engine /v1/models failed: {e}\")\n\n\n@app.api_route(\"/v1/{path:path}\", methods=[\"GET\", \"POST\", \"PUT\", \"DELETE\", \"OPTIONS\"])\nasync def proxy_v1(path: str, request: Request):\n    \"\"\"Transparent OpenAI-compatible proxy to the mlx_lm.server child. Cold-starts\n    the child if needed, streams the response (stream=true SSE works), and tracks\n    in-flight requests so idle-unload can't kill a live generation.\"\"\"\n    global _active, _last_request_at\n    _check_auth(request)\n    await _ensure_started()\n    body = await request.body()\n    headers = {k: v for k, v in request.headers.items()\n               if k.lower() not in (\"host\", \"content-length\", \"authorization\")}\n    url = f\"{CHILD_BASE}/v1/{path}\"\n    client = httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=None)\n    _active += 1\n    try:\n        req = client.build_request(request.method, url, headers=headers,\n                                   content=body, params=request.query_params)\n        resp = await client.send(req, stream=True)\n    except Exception as e:\n        _active -= 1\n        _last_request_at = time.monotonic()\n        await client.aclose()\n        raise HTTPException(502, f\"engine proxy failed: {e}\")\n\n    async def streamer():\n        global _active, _last_request_at\n        try:\n            async for chunk in resp.aiter_raw():\n                yield chunk\n        finally:\n            await resp.aclose()\n            await client.aclose()\n            _active -= 1\n            _last_request_at = time.monotonic()\n\n    passthru = {k: v for k, v in resp.headers.items()\n                if k.lower() not in (\"content-length\", \"transfer-encoding\", \"connection\")}\n    return StreamingResponse(streamer(), status_code=resp.status_code,\n                             headers=passthru, media_type=resp.headers.get(\"content-type\"))\n"}

The 404 was my test's fault, not the wrapper — mlx_lm.server registers the model under its **full ref** (the path), and it even auto-discovers other HF-cache models (it listed the dia model). {"file_path":"/Users/gyasisutton/Documents/code/atelier/sidecars/mlxlm/README.md","content":"# mlxlm-sidecar — LLM via Apple mlx_lm.server (MLX-native, Metal)\n\nA thin **managed wrapper** around [`mlx_lm.server`](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm) — Apple's official MLX LLM server. Port **8773**. The MLX-native LLM path; typically faster than GGUF on Apple Silicon, and it tracks the mlx-lm release exactly.\n\n> This is the working MLX-native sidecar. The **fastmlx** sidecar (`:8772`) is scaffolded but blocked on upstream FastMLX lagging mlx-lm's API (it imports/calls removed symbols like `generate_step(temp=…)`); re-enable it when FastMLX catches up.\n\n```\nclient → :8773/v1/chat/completions      (Atelier-fronted OpenAI API)\n         :8773/healthz /readyz /agent /admin/unload\n         └─ proxies → 127.0.0.1:18773    (mlx_lm.server child, MLX/Metal)\nidle → wrapper stops the child → MLX model memory freed.\n```\n\nmlx_lm.server loads **one model at startup** (`--model`), so cold-start = model load; \"warm\" = model loaded.\n\n## Install / deploy\n\n`requirements.txt` pulls `mlx` + `mlx-lm` (the engine) + the FastAPI/httpx wrapper stack. `deploy/install.sh` creates the venv, symlinks `server.py`, and drops the plist. Set `MLXLM_MODEL` to an `mlx-community` repo or a local model dir.\n\n## Use (OpenAI-compatible)\n\n```sh\ncurl -s http://192.168.0.159:8773/v1/chat/completions -H 'content-type: application/json' \\\n  -d '{\"model\":\"<MLXLM_MODEL ref>\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hello\"}]}'\n\n# streaming\ncurl -sN http://192.168.0.159:8773/v1/chat/completions -H 'content-type: application/json' \\\n  -d '{\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hi\"}],\"stream\":true}'   # model optional → uses loaded one\n```\n\n> **Model field:** mlx_lm.server registers the model under its `--model` ref (repo name or local path) and also auto-discovers other models in `HF_HOME`. Send `\"model\"` = the exact `MLXLM_MODEL` ref, **or omit it** (uses the loaded model). Sending a different id makes it try to load that model.\n\n## Lifecycle\n\n| Endpoint | Purpose |\n|---|---|\n| `GET /healthz` | liveness (wrapper only) |\n| `GET /readyz` | warm/cold/busy, child pid, model |\n| `GET /agent` | machine-readable manifest for agents |\n| `POST /admin/unload[?force=true]` | stop the engine to free MLX memory |\n| `ANY /v1/{path}` | OpenAI proxy (cold-starts the engine on first call) |\n\nCold-starts on the first `/v1` call, **idle-unloads** after `IDLE_UNLOAD_SECONDS` (default 600). In-flight requests are tracked so idle-unload never interrupts a live generation.\n\n## Env vars\n\n| Var | Default |\n|---|---|\n| `MLXLM_MODEL` | — (required: mlx-community repo or local dir) |\n| `MLXLM_ALIAS` | model basename (display name) |\n| `MLXLM_PYTHON` | the wrapper's interpreter (has mlx-lm) |\n| `MLXLM_PORT` | `8773` (public) |\n| `MLXLM_CHILD_PORT` | `18773` (internal mlx_lm.server) |\n| `MLXLM_ARGS` | extra mlx_lm.server args |\n| `IDLE_UNLOAD_SECONDS` | `600` |\n| `KEEP_WARM` | `false` |\n| `HF_HUB_OFFLINE` | set `1` when `MLXLM_MODEL` is a local dir |\n| `HUB_TOKEN` | unset |\n\n> MLX-native path. For GGUF models use the **llamacpp** sidecar (`:8771`).\n"}

## Where this landed

**Two working LLM sidecars now in the hub:**
- **llamacpp** (`:8771`) — GGUF/Metal, running your **gemma4:12b**
- **mlxlm** (`:8773`) — MLX-native via Apple's `mlx_lm.server`, verified with Qwen2.5-0.5B

**FastMLX** (`:8772`) stays scaffolded but **honestly flagged as blocked** — its role in the governor says `[blocked: upstream]`, and both its README and ATELIER.md explain why (FastMLX 0.2.1 calls removed mlx-lm APIs like `generate_step(temp=…)`; re-enable when upstream catches up). I left its patched `utils.py` as-is but didn't pursue the deeper generation-code fork.

**Full hub wiring done** for mlxlm: governor (BASE/LABELS/ROLES/AGENT_CAPABLE), launchd plist, README, install.sh venv loop + verify port, doctor.sh, dashboard (`get_sidecars`/`SIDECAR_MEM`/mock), ATELIER.md. All compiles/validates.

## Use it
```sh
# MLX-native (mlxlm)
curl -s http://192.168.0.159:8773/v1/chat/completions -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"..."}]}'        # model optional → loaded model

# GGUF (llamacpp, gemma4:12b)

  -d '{"model":"gemma4-12b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"..."}],"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":false}}'
```

- The mlxlm plist points at the small Qwen2.5-0.5B I downloaded for the test — swap `MLXLM_MODEL` to whatever MLX model you want (e.g. an `mlx-community` 8B–14B; with the HF network issue you'd curl it down like before, or drop `HF_HUB_OFFLINE` once that's resolved).

Now I've got the full picture. Here's my recommendation, then the doc you referenced.

## For movable/dockable panels: **Gridstack.js**

Your dashboard is currently a hardcoded 3×2 CSS grid (Resident Memory · Tenants/Sidecars · Task Stream / Loaded Now · Inference Latency · Sidecar Status). To make those panels user-movable tiles, **Gridstack.js** is the right fit:

- **Vanilla, zero-dependency, ~10 KB** — works with your plain-JS Tauri webview (no React needed), and **vendors as a local file** so the app stays fully offline (same pattern as your local `chart.js`).
- Does exactly what you described: **drag to move, drag-edge to resize, snap-to-grid tiles, and serialize/restore the layout** (save to `localStorage` or a Tauri file so it persists across launches).
- It's the **vanilla equivalent of what Apache Superset uses** (Superset is `react-grid-layout`; Gridstack is the framework-agnostic sibling).

**When you'd want something else:** if you need true **Photoshop/IDE docking** — tab stacks, nested splits, pop-out windows — that's **Golden Layout** or **Dockview**. But those are heavier and a different mental model (window management, steeper learning curve). For a monitoring dashboard of rearrangeable tiles, Gridstack is the proportionate choice; Golden Layout is overkill.

**What I'd implement:** wrap each existing panel in a Gridstack widget, add an "✎ Edit layout / 🔒 Lock" toggle (drag/resize only in edit mode), and persist the layout. Charts (Chart.js) re-flow on resize via Gridstack's `resizestop` event. No backend changes — it's all in `dashboard/ui/`.

Target: `dashboard/ui/` only — no Rust/backend changes.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Library decision — Gridstack.js\n\n| Option | Verdict |\n|---|---|\n| **Gridstack.js** ✅ | Vanilla TS/JS, **zero dependencies**, ~10 KB, drag + resize + snap-to-grid + **serialize/restore** layout, responsive breakpoints. Vendors as a local file → keeps the Tauri app **offline**. The framework-agnostic equivalent of what Apache Superset uses (`react-grid-layout`). The proportionate choice for a dashboard of rearrangeable tiles. |\n| Golden Layout / Dockview | True IDE/Photoshop **docking** — tab stacks, nested splits, pop-out windows. Heavier, steeper, different mental model (window management). Revisit only if we need tabs/nesting, not for tiles. |\n\n**Pick: Gridstack.js.** Offline-vendorable, vanilla (our webview is plain JS + Chart.js, no React), and it does exactly drag/resize/persist.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Current state (what we're converting)\n\nTwo hardcoded CSS grids in `dashboard/ui/index.html`:\n\n- `.app` (top): `grid-template-columns: 1.15fr 1fr 1.25fr`\n- `.hud` (footer): `grid-template-columns: 0.85fr 1.15fr 1.25fr`\n\nSix panels (`data-od-id` preserved for the OpenDesign source mapping):\n\n| Panel `data-od-id` | Contents | Chart canvas |\n|---|---|---|\n| `memory-panel` | Resident Memory big-readout + chart | `#memChart` |\n| `tenants-panel` | Tenants/Sidecars tile grid (`#tenantGrid`) | — |\n| `tasks-panel` | Task Stream: activity gantt + table | — |\n| `hud-pie` | Loaded-now pie + legend | `#pieChart` |\n| `hud-lines` | Inference latency (TTFT) + generation tok/s | `#ttftChart`, `#tpsChart` |\n| `hud-status` | Sidecar status table | — |\n\n4 Chart.js charts total — these need an explicit resize hook (Chart.js doesn't auto-reflow inside a Gridstack resize).\n\n---\n\n## 3. Target design\n\n- Each `<section class=\"panel\" data-od-id=\"…\">` becomes a **Gridstack widget**: wrapped in `.grid-stack-item > .grid-stack-item-content`, with `gs-x / gs-y / gs-w / gs-h` initial coords (12-column grid).\n- One `.grid-stack` container replaces both CSS grids (panels can move freely between the old top/bottom regions).\n- **Edit/Lock toggle** (a small `✎ / 🔒` button in the header): `grid.setStatic(true|false)`. Default **locked** so normal viewing doesn't accidentally drag; unlock to rearrange.\n- **Persistence:** on `grid.on('change')`, save `grid.save(false)` (layout only, no content) to `localStorage[\"atelier.layout.v1\"]`; restore on load. (Later: persist to a Tauri file via a `save_layout` command so it survives reinstalls and syncs the HUD window.)\n- **Reset layout** button → clear storage, re-apply the default coords.\n\nDefault coordinate map (12-col, ~6 rows; mirrors the current arrangement):\n\n```\nmemory-panel   x0  y0  w4 h4      tenants-panel  x4 y0 w4 h4    tasks-panel x8 y0 w4 h8\nhud-pie        x0  y4  w4 h4      hud-lines      x4 y4 w4 h4    hud-status  x8 y8 w4 h4\n```\n\n---\n\n## 4. Implementation steps\n\n1. **Vendor Gridstack offline** — download into `dashboard/ui/vendor/`:\n   - `gridstack-all.js` (UMD bundle, ~v11.x)\n   - `gridstack.min.css`\n   Add `<link>` + `<script>` tags to `index.html` (local paths, no CDN — matches the existing local `vendor/chart.umd.min.js`).\n2. **Restructure markup** — wrap the 6 panels in `.grid-stack` / `.grid-stack-item` with initial `gs-*` attrs. Keep each panel's inner DOM (and `data-od-id`) intact so `refreshAll()`'s selectors (`[data-od-id=\"tenants-panel\"] …`, `#tenantGrid`, canvas ids) keep working unchanged.\n3. **Init Gridstack** — `GridStack.init({ column: 12, cellHeight: '7vh', float: true, margin: 6, staticGrid: true, handle: '.panel-drag' })`. Add a tiny drag handle in each panel header.\n4. **Edit/Lock toggle** — button flips `grid.setStatic()`; show a subtle \"edit mode\" outline when unlocked.\n5. **Chart.js resize** — `grid.on('resizestop', (e, el) => { el.querySelectorAll('canvas').forEach(c => Chart.getChart(c)?.resize()); })`. Also resize on `change` for programmatic moves.\n6. **Persist + restore** — `grid.on('change', saveLayout)`; on boot, if stored layout exists, `grid.load(stored)` before wiring data; else apply defaults.\n7. **Theme** — override Gridstack's default CSS (resize handles, placeholder) to the dark/gold palette so it matches the OD design. Keep panel borders/headers as-is.\n8. **HUD window** — `hud.html` is a separate webview; give it its own (smaller) default layout + storage key, or leave it fixed for v1.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Risks / notes\n\n- **Chart reflow** is the main gotcha — verified hook is `resizestop` + `Chart.resize()`. Without it charts keep their old pixel size.\n- **`data-od-id` must survive** — they map back to the OpenDesign prototype; don't strip them when wrapping.\n- **Embedded HUD iframe** (`#hudIframe`) sits inside the layout — treat it as a normal widget or pin it.\n- Offline: never reference a CDN at runtime; vendor everything (the app is a sealed `.app`).\n- No backend impact — this is purely `dashboard/ui/` + one optional Tauri `save_layout`/`load_layout` command later for file-based persistence.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Future\n\n- File-based layout persistence via a Tauri command (survives reinstalls; shareable presets).\n- Multiple named layouts (\"monitoring\", \"debug\", \"compact\") with a switcher.\n- If tabs/nesting/pop-out windows are ever wanted → migrate to **Golden Layout** or **Dockview** (bigger lift; only if the tile model proves too limiting).\n\nSources: [Gridstack.js](https://gridstackjs.com/) · [github.com/gridstack/gridstack.js](https://github.com/gridstack/gridstack.js/) · [JS grid layouts 2026 (Sencha)](https://www.sencha.com/blog/must-try-javascript-grid-layouts-for-modern-web-design/)\n"}

**Recommendation: Gridstack.js** for the Photoshop/Superset-style movable panels. It's the right call for your setup because it's:
- **Vanilla, zero-dep, ~10 KB** — fits your plain-JS Tauri webview (no React), and **vendors as a local file** so the app stays fully offline (same pattern as your local `chart.js`)
- Purpose-built for **drag-move, edge-resize, snap-to-grid tiles with save/restore** — the vanilla equivalent of what Apache Superset uses (`react-grid-layout`)
- *(Golden Layout / Dockview only if you later want true IDE docking — tabs, nested splits, pop-outs — which is a heavier, different model)*

- 8 implementation steps, all in `dashboard/ui/` — **no backend changes**
- Risks called out (chart reflow, preserving `data-od-id`, offline vendoring, the HUD iframe)

Sources: [Gridstack.js](https://gridstackjs.com/) · [github](https://github.com/gridstack/gridstack.js/) · [JS grid layouts 2026](https://www.sencha.com/blog/must-try-javascript-grid-layouts-for-modern-web-design/)

[el] : document.querySelectorAll('.grid-stack-item')).forEach(it =>\n      it.querySelectorAll('canvas').forEach(c => window.Chart?.getChart?.(c)?.resize()));\n  const saveLayout = () => {\n    try { localStorage.setItem(LS_KEY, JSON.stringify(grid.save(false))); } catch {}\n  };\n  const fitHeight = () => grid.cellHeight(Math.floor(window.innerHeight / 12));\n  window.addEventListener('resize', () => { fitHeight(); resizeCharts(); });\n\n  // restore a saved arrangement\n  try {\n    const saved = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(LS_KEY) || 'null');\n    if (Array.isArray(saved) && saved.length) grid.load(saved);\n  } catch {}\n\n  grid.on('resizestop', (e, el) => resizeCharts(el));\n  grid.on('change', () => { resizeCharts(); saveLayout(); });\n\n  // toolbar: Edit/Lock + Reset\n  const bar = document.createElement('div');\n  bar.className = 'layout-bar';\n  const editBtn = document.createElement('button');\n  editBtn.textContent = '✎ Edit Layout';\n  const resetBtn = document.createElement('button');\n  resetBtn.textContent = '⟲ Reset';\n  bar.append(editBtn, resetBtn);\n  document.body.appendChild(bar);\n\n  let editing = false;\n  editBtn.addEventListener('click', () => {\n    editing = !editing;\n    grid.setStatic(!editing);\n    document.body.classList.toggle('layout-edit', editing);\n    editBtn.classList.toggle('active', editing);\n    editBtn.textContent = editing ? '🔒 Lock Layout' : '✎ Edit Layout';\n    if (!editing) saveLayout();\n    resizeCharts();\n  });\n  resetBtn.addEventListener('click', () => { localStorage.removeItem(LS_KEY); location.reload(); });\n\n  requestAnimationFrame(() => { fitHeight(); resizeCharts(); });\n})();"}

_**Agent (2026-06-06 13:42:04Z)**_

Rebuilt and relaunched (pid 3544) — the new drag/resize UX is live in the app.

## What's now in the dashboard

**Click `✎ Edit Layout`** (bottom-left) and you'll get unmistakable affordances:

- **Top gold banner** spells out the controls
- **⠿ grip + highlighted header** on each panel → drag the header to **move** it
- **Gold edge strips** on all four sides: **left/right = X-resize**, **top/bottom = Y-resize**, plus **corner squares** for both axes at once
- Dashed gold outlines so you can see every panel's bounds

**Behaviors (gridstack, verified):**
- **Snap** — moves and resizes snap to the 12-column grid
- **Push** — drag a panel over another and it **shoves the others out of the way** (tested: dragging Memory onto Tenants pushed Tenants down)
- **Min-size** — panels can't be shrunk so small the content breaks (minW 3, minH 3)
- **Persist** — your arrangement saves automatically; `⟲ Reset` restores the default

**Click `🔒 Lock Layout`** when done — handles/grips disappear, panels are static for normal viewing, and the layout is saved.

Give it a try in the live app: hit Edit, grab a header by the **⠿**, drop it on another panel to watch them reshuffle, then drag the **gold edge strips** to resize on X or Y. If you want different defaults (starting arrangement, min sizes, strip thickness, or panels that swap instead of push), tell me and I'll tune it — this is the annotate-and-adjust loop working.

Width stays per-panel.\n  let _startH = null;\n  grid.on('resizestart', (e, el) => { _startH = el.gridstackNode.h; });\n  grid.on('resizestop', (e, el) => {\n    const n = el.gridstackNode;\n    if (_startH != null && n.h !== _startH) {\n      grid.batchUpdate();\n      grid.getGridItems().forEach(other => {\n        const on = other.gridstackNode;\n        if (other !== el && on.y === n.y && on.h !== n.h) grid.update(other, { h: n.h });\n      });\n      grid.batchUpdate(false);   // commit — float:false then pushes the row below down\n    }\n    _startH = null;\n    resizeCharts(el);\n    saveLayout();\n  });\n  grid.on('change', () => { resizeCharts(); saveLayout(); });"}

That's the "don't resize the same" issue. Let me make them **auto-fit** so they form even rows that adapt to the panel width:

_**Agent (2026-06-06 15:07:33Z)**_

<details><summary>Tool use: <b>Edit</b></summary>


_**Agent (2026-06-06 15:51:40Z)**_

Understood — the hard rule: **nothing ever gets pushed outside the visible window.** No matter how you resize, the whole layout must always fit — no panel shoved below the fold, no scrolling. The problem now: growing one row pushes the other row *down* past the bottom. The fix is **complementary resize** — when one row grows, the other shrinks to match, so the total always equals the viewport — plus a hard `maxRow` cap as a safety net.

First, cap the grid so it can never exceed the viewport rows:

Two layers now guarantee the layout **always fits the visible window**, no matter how you resize:

1. **Complementary resize** — growing one row automatically shrinks the other so they always sum to the full viewport. Verified: dragging the top row to h10 shrank the bottom row to h2 → total stays 12 rows = the window. The bottom row can never get pushed below the fold.
2. **Hard `maxRow` cap** — gridstack physically refuses any move/resize that would exceed the viewport's rows. Plus `overflow:hidden` on the container as a final backstop.
3. **Min-row floor** — neither row can collapse below 2 cells, so a panel can't be crushed to nothing.

And the **cells recompute on window resize**, so if you resize the *window*, all 12 rows re-fit to the new height — panels scale, never spill.

Combined with the earlier fixes, the dashboard now behaves like a proper bounded workspace:
- **3×2 default** that fills the screen
- **Move** panels by the ⠿ header (snap + push)
- **Resize a row** → its row-mates match and the opposite row gives up space — everything stays on-screen
- **Sidecar tiles** reflow into even columns as their panel widens
- **Lock/Reset**, layout persists
- One command (`deploy/install-dashboard.sh`) keeps the installed app current

It's live in the app now. Resize a row all the way up — you'll see the other row compress to keep everything visible, and it'll never scroll or push a panel out of sight. If you hit any case where something *does* slip off-screen, redpen-circle it and I'll clamp that path too.

Here's my understanding — confirm and I'll build it:

## Width-complementary resize (the horizontal twin of the row-height behavior)

**When you resize one panel's *width* in a row, the other panels in that row resize to absorb the leftover space, split equally — so the row always fills the full width (12 columns), never overflowing and never leaving a gap.**

Concretely:
- A row has 3 panels at **w4 + w4 + w4 = 12** (full width).
- You drag panel 1's side edge to **w6**.
- Remaining width = 12 − 6 = **6**, divided **equally** among the other two → **w3 each**.
- Result: **6 + 3 + 3 = 12** — row still spans the full width, no overflow, no gap.
- Same idea if you shrink one: the others **grow equally** to refill the freed space.

Details I'd apply:
- **Same row only** (the panel's row-mates), mirroring the height logic by band.
- **Equal split** of the leftover among the *non-resized* siblings.
- **Min-width floor** (e.g. 2 columns) so no sibling collapses to nothing — if the resize would push a sibling below the floor, the resized panel is clamped.
- Row stays pinned to **12 columns** total → never spills past the window width, never leaves dead space.
- Combined with the existing height rule, **both axes are now bounded**: resize anything and the row/column rebalances so the whole grid always fits the viewport exactly.

Yes — and good call to lock the limits down first. Here's the **sizing-limit spec** I'll enforce (all tunable constants):

## Size limits (both axes always fill, never overflow, never collapse)

| Constraint | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Row width** | always **= 12 columns** | full window width, no gap, no spill |
| **Total height** | always **= 12 rows** | full viewport height |
| **Min panel width** | **2 cols** (~⅙ width) | a panel can't be crushed to a sliver |
| **Min row height** | **2 cells** | a row can't collapse to nothing |
| **Max panel width** (row of N) | **12 − (N−1)×2** | leaves every sibling ≥ min · 3-up row → max **8**, 2-up → max **10**, alone → 12 |
| **Max row height** (2 rows) | **12 − 2 = 10** | leaves the other row ≥ min |
| **At a limit** | **clamp** | the dragged panel stops; siblings hold at min — no overflow, no collapse |

**Behavior:** drag a side edge → that panel takes the new width (clamped to max), the **other panels in its row split the leftover equally** (each ≥ 2 cols), and the row re-tiles to exactly 12. Shrink one → others grow equally. Height already works this way between the two rows. So both axes are bounded: **resize anything and the row/column rebalances to fill the viewport exactly — nothing ever leaves the visible area.**

_**Agent (2026-06-06 16:07:49Z)**_

Built, installed, and relaunched (Jun 6 18:07). The width-complementary resize with full size limits is live.

## What you can do now — both axes bounded, always fits

**Width resize (new):** drag a panel's **side edge** → that panel takes the new width, and the **other panels in its row split the leftover equally**, re-tiling to exactly 12 columns. Verified: Memory → w7 made Tenants w3 + Tasks w2 (row stays full-width, no gap, no spill).

**The size limits you asked me to lock down (all enforced):**

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Row width | always **12 cols** (full width) |
| Total height | always **12 rows** (full viewport) |
| Min panel width | **2 cols** |
| Min row height | **2 cells** |
| Max panel width (3-up row) | **8** (leaves 2+2 for siblings) |
| Max row height (2 rows) | **10** (leaves 2 for the other) |
| At a limit | **clamp** — dragged panel stops, siblings hold at min |

So now, whatever you grab:
- **Side edge** → row redistributes width equally, fills 12 cols
- **Top/bottom edge** → the two rows trade height, fill 12 rows
- Hit a limit → it clamps; nothing ever collapses to nothing or spills past the window

The whole grid is a sealed workspace — **resize anything and it rebalances to fill the viewport exactly, never overflowing**. Implementation note: I apply the recomputed layout with `grid.load()` (atomic) instead of incremental updates, which is what made the last column behave.

Give it a spin in the app: Edit Layout → drag Memory's right edge wider; Tenants and Task Stream shrink evenly to keep the row full. If you'd prefer the leftover split **proportionally** (keep relative sizes) instead of equally, that's a one-line change — say the word.

_**Agent (2026-06-06 16:12:51Z)**_

Here's what I think you mean — tell me if I've got it:

## My understanding

**When you drag a panel and it *overlaps* another panel (drop it onto an occupied spot), it should NOT push the other panels around.**

Right now, gridstack's move behavior is "push" — if you drag a panel on top of another, it shoves the others out of the way, which can cascade and bump a panel into a new row → exactly the kind of overflow/displacement we've been killing. You want the opposite: **dragging a panel onto another should just *swap* the two** (they trade places), so the grid stays the clean, fully-filled 2×3 (or whatever) layout and **nothing gets pushed off into overflow**.

So:
- **Move panel A onto panel B's spot** → A and B **swap positions** (A takes B's place, B takes A's). No third panel gets shoved, no row grows, the layout stays bounded and fills the viewport.
- Contrast with today: dropping A on B *pushes* B (and maybe others) down/around, which can overflow.

In short: **collision on move = swap, not push.** That keeps the "everything always fits, nothing leaves the view" guarantee for *moving* panels, the same way the complementary resize keeps it for *resizing*.

**Is that right?** If yes, I'll switch the drag behavior so overlapping a panel swaps them (instead of pushing), and verify a move never displaces anything out of the grid.

If you actually meant something else — e.g. "a dragged panel shouldn't be *allowed* to overlap at all (it snaps back if it can't fit)", or you were confirming the resize no-push — point me at it and I'll restate.

- **Grab an edge/corner** (resize region) → **push / complementary fill** (rows & columns rebalance — already built)
- **Grab the panel body/header** (move region) → **SWAP**: drop it onto another panel and the two **exchange grid slots** — no pushing, so the tiling stays intact and can never overflow

So the grid has fixed slots; moving a panel onto another just swaps which slot each occupies. Let me implement swap-on-move:

## Region-aware behavior — both gestures, both bounded

| You grab… | Region | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| **Panel edge/corner** | resize | **Push / complementary fill** — rows trade height, row-mates split width equally; always fills 12×12, never overflows |
| **Panel body/header** (⠿) | move | **Swap** — drop onto another panel and they **exchange slots**; nobody else moves, tiling stays intact |

**Swap-on-move, verified:** dropping Memory onto Task Stream made them trade places (Memory → top-right, Task Stream → top-left), with all four other panels untouched and the grid still filling exactly 12 rows. No cascading push, so a move can never shove a panel off-screen.

So the dashboard is now a fully **sealed, region-aware workspace**:
- **Move** (grab body) = swap slots → layout never breaks
- **Resize** (grab edge) = complementary fill → rows/columns rebalance to the viewport
- Size limits clamp (min 2 cols/rows; max leaves siblings ≥ min)
- Everything always fits; nothing ever pushed out of view
- `deploy/install-dashboard.sh` keeps the installed app in sync

It's live — try it: Edit Layout → grab a panel by its **⠿ header** and drop it on another (they swap); grab an **edge** to resize (the row rebalances).

_**Agent (2026-06-06 16:53:34Z)**_

Here's what I think you mean — confirm before I build it:

## My understanding: borders-as-splitters (gutter resize)

Instead of resize **handles attached to each panel's edge**, make the **shared border *between* two panels** the drag handle — like the splitter bars in an IDE or a tiling window manager.

- **Drag the vertical divider** between two side-by-side panels → it slides left/right, **widening one panel and narrowing its neighbor** by the same amount. The row stays exactly full-width.
- **Drag the horizontal divider** between the top and bottom rows → it slides up/down, **trading height between the two rows**. The column stays exactly full-height.

**Why this "solves the resize issue":** a divider just *moves the boundary* between two adjacent panels, so the space it takes from one it gives to the other — the complementary fill is **automatic and exact**, with no separate handle elements, no per-panel clamping math, and no chance of overflow or the gridstack-scramble I kept fighting. You grab the seam, you slide it, the two sides rebalance. It's the natural, predictable resize model.

So:
- **Borders = resize splitters** (drag the seam → the two adjacent panels trade space)
- **Panel body/header = move** (swap slots — already done)
- Edges no longer have their own little handles; the seam between panels *is* the handle.

**Is that it?** If yes, I'll overlay draggable gutters on the seams (vertical seams between columns, the horizontal seam between rows), and on drag compute the new split and apply it via `grid.load()` so it stays bounded and exact.

One thing to decide: a vertical seam in a 3-column row sits between *two specific panels* — should dragging it resize **just those two** (left + right neighbor trade, third panel untouched), or the classic split behavior? I'd default to **just the two panels touching that seam** trade space — most intuitive. Good?

_**Agent (2026-06-06 17:26:26Z)**_

Built, installed, relaunched (Jun 6 19:26). The seam/gutter resize is live.

## What I built — borders-as-handles, row equalizes

You now resize by **dragging the seam between panels** (no per-panel handles):

- **Vertical seam** (border between two side-by-side panels) → drag it; the panel on the left takes the new width, and **all the other panels in that row resize to the *same* width** to fill the rest. Verified: drag Memory's seam → Memory w6, Tenants + Tasks both w3, row = 12.
- **Horizontal seam** (border between the two rows) → drag it; the two rows **trade height**, column stays full.
- Seams glow gold on hover in edit mode; cursor is `col-resize`/`row-resize`.

This is exactly the model you wanted, and it inherently "solves the resize issue": moving a boundary takes from one side and gives to the rest evenly, so it **always sums to the full grid — no overflow, no scramble**, and the math is trivial.

The complete interaction set, region-aware:
- **Grab the seam/border** → resize (row redistributes to equal widths / rows trade height)
- **Grab the panel header (⠿)** → move = **swap** with the panel you drop on
- **Limits**: min 2 cols/rows, the dragged panel clamps so siblings never go below min
- Everything always fills the viewport; nothing ever pushed out of view
- Lock/Reset, persists; `install-dashboard.sh` keeps the app current

Try it in the app: **Edit Layout** → hover a border (it glows) → drag it; the two/three panels rebalance evenly. Grab a header to swap panels.

Honest caveat: I verified the seam drag with a synthesized pointer drag (passed cleanly). Real trackpad feel can differ slightly — if the live resize feels jumpy while dragging, I can throttle the `grid.load` to animation frames for smoothness. Tell me how it feels.

_**Agent (2026-06-06 17:30:56Z)**_

Now I can see the bug — the panels have scrambled into a weird stacked arrangement (Memory tall on the left, Loaded Now stacked under it, Tenants/Task Stream crammed right). And your diagnosis is exactly right: **it's gridstack's auto-ordering/collision engine (`float:false`) fighting my explicit layout.** When a resize produces any intermediate overlap, gridstack "helpfully" reflows panels into other rows → the jumping and weird ordering.

The fix is to make **my code the sole authority** on positions — switch gridstack to `float:true` so it places panels exactly where I tell it and never auto-rearranges. Let me address both your points:

**Bug #1 — stop the row-jumping** (gridstack authoritative):

_**Agent (2026-06-06 17:33:40Z)**_

I see it — and your "weird ordering system" diagnosis is dead on. The deeper problem isn't just `float`: my code **reads panel positions back from gridstack between gestures**, and gridstack's engine doesn't always report them consistently, so each new resize starts from a corrupted snapshot → panels jump rows, rows end up with 2 or 4 panels. Patching gridstack's engine has been whack-a-mole.

**The right fix is a real refactor:** keep my *own* layout model as the single source of truth (rows → ordered panels with widths, + the two row heights), and render it to gridstack deterministically. Never read back. This kills the ordering/jumping bug **and** makes "insert between" (your #2) trivial. Let me read the current layout code so I rewrite it cleanly:
